The review follows the **PRISMA framework** for systematic reviews. Databases searched: IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer, and ACM Digital Library. Inclusion criteria:

• Focus on **SAC in 5G/B5G network slicing**
• Explicit **revenue or profit maximization objective**
• Quantitative evaluation of admission policies

From 142 initial results, 23 studies met all criteria. Data extracted includes:

• **Optimization objective** (e.g., long-term revenue, SLA penalty minimization)
• **Slice elasticity model** (rigid vs. elastic resource demand)
• **Algorithm type**: heuristic, ILP, RL, game theory
• **Key performance indicators**: acceptance ratio, revenue per time unit, resource utilization

Thematic analysis was used to categorize approaches and identify research gaps.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Key findings from the 23 studies:

✅ **87%** (20/23) model slices as **elastic**, allowing dynamic resource scaling based on price or demand.
✅ **Reinforcement Learning (RL)** is the dominant approach (9 studies), followed by **Integer Linear Programming (ILP)** (7 studies) and **heuristics** (5 studies).
✅ Top revenue drivers: **dynamic pricing**, **slice preemption with compensation**, and **multi-period resource reservation**.
✅ Only **3 studies** consider **energy cost** in revenue calculation—highlighting a major gap.

The highest reported revenue gain was **+38%** over baseline first-come-first-served admission, achieved via **deep Q-learning with SLA-aware reward shaping**. However, most studies assume **perfect demand forecasting**, limiting real-world applicability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content:
This review confirms that **revenue-aware SAC is a mature yet evolving field**, with RL emerging as the most adaptive solution for dynamic 5G markets. However, critical gaps remain: **lack of standard evaluation benchmarks**, **neglect of operational costs** (e.g., energy, maintenance), and **limited integration with end-to-end slice lifecycle management**.

Future work should focus on **real-world pilot validations**, **federated learning for multi-operator SAC**, and **green revenue models** that balance profit with sustainability. Standardized datasets and open-source SAC simulators are urgently needed to accelerate progress.

title: Macro-level Energy Demand Analysis Based on Bottom-up Information for Telecommunication Networks: A Case Study of Indonesia
author: Mochamad Mardi Marta Dinata, Yohei Yamaguchi, Hideaki Uchida, Yoshiyuki Shimoda, Agus Subekti

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
**Telecommunication infrastructure** is a critical enabler of digital transformation, especially in archipelagic nations like **Indonesia**, where over **70,000 Base Transceiver Stations (BTS)** serve a population of more than 270 million. However, the energy consumption of these BTS—often powered by diesel generators in remote areas—poses significant **economic, environmental, and logistical challenges**.

This study addresses the urgent need for **sustainable energy planning** by developing a **macro-level energy demand model** derived from **bottom-up BTS data**, including location, power rating, operational hours, and grid connectivity status. Such granular data enables precise estimation of national energy requirements and informs the design of **hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES)** tailored to local conditions.

With Indonesia’s commitment to achieving **23% renewable energy in its national mix by 2025**, this research provides a data-driven foundation for integrating solar, wind, and battery storage into telecom networks—reducing carbon emissions and operational costs while enhancing energy resilience.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
The research employed a **bottom-up aggregation approach** using real-world BTS datasets provided by Indonesia’s Ministry of Communication and Informatics and major telecom operators. Key steps included:

• **Data collection**: Geolocation, power capacity (kW), backup system type, and grid dependency for 68,421 BTS across 34 provinces.
• **Energy profiling**: Hourly load estimation based on equipment specifications (e.g., 2G/4G/5G radios, cooling systems).
• **Spatial clustering**: Grouping BTS by region, terrain (urban/coastal/mountainous), and energy access to identify deployment patterns.
• **Demand aggregation**: Summing individual BTS loads to derive provincial and national energy demand curves.
• **Hybrid system simulation**: Using **HOMER Pro** to model solar-diesel-battery configurations for representative BTS clusters, optimizing for **Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE)** and **renewable fraction**.

Sensitivity analyses were conducted for solar irradiance variability, battery degradation, and fuel price fluctuations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
The analysis revealed that Indonesia’s telecom network consumes approximately **1.2 TWh/year**, with **42%** of BTS located in off-grid or weak-grid areas relying on diesel. Key findings include:

✅ **National peak demand**: ~185 MW, concentrated in Java and Sumatra.
✅ **Renewable potential**: Over **60%** of off-grid BTS can achieve >80% solar fraction with <15% LCOE increase compared to diesel-only systems.
✅ **CO₂ reduction**: Full hybridization could cut emissions by **~850,000 tons/year**.

Case studies in East Nusa Tenggara and Papua demonstrated **LCOE reductions of 22–35%** using optimized PV-battery-diesel systems. The bottom-up model also identified **12 high-priority provinces** for immediate renewable integration based on diesel dependency and solar resource availability.

The macro-demand model achieved **>92% accuracy** when validated against operator-reported energy consumption data.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content:
This study proves that **bottom-up BTS data** is a powerful basis for **national-scale energy planning** in the telecom sector. By translating granular infrastructure data into actionable macro-level insights, policymakers and operators can strategically deploy **hybrid renewable systems** that are both **economically viable** and **environmentally sustainable**.

The methodology is scalable to other developing countries facing similar energy-access challenges. Future work includes:

• Integration of **5G densification trends** and their energy implications.
• Real-time **AI-driven load forecasting** for dynamic energy management.
• Policy frameworks for **shared renewable infrastructure** among telecom operators.

Ultimately, this approach supports Indonesia’s green digital economy vision while ensuring **universal, resilient connectivity**.

title: Pengenalan Big Data Dan Pembuatan Aplikasi Database Dengan NocoDB Pada Badan Santunan Yatim Pondok Cina Depok
author: Muhammad Bagus Andra Andra, Eni Heni Hermaliani, Agus Subekti Subekti, Muhammad Haris Haris

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
Lembaga sosial seperti **Badan Santunan Yatim Pondok Cina Depok** seringkali mengelola data penerima manfaat, donatur, keuangan, dan kegiatan secara manual atau dengan spreadsheet, yang rentan terhadap **kesalahan, duplikasi, dan ketidakefisienan**. Di era digital, pemanfaatan teknologi informasi menjadi kunci untuk **transparansi, akuntabilitas, dan skalabilitas** layanan sosial.

Kegiatan pengabdian ini memperkenalkan konsep **Big Data** secara sederhana—fokus pada volume, kecepatan, dan variasi data dalam konteks lembaga yatim—dan memberikan pelatihan praktis pembuatan **aplikasi database tanpa coding** menggunakan **NocoDB**, sebuah platform open-source yang mengubah spreadsheet menjadi sistem manajemen database berbasis web.

Tujuannya adalah **memberdayakan staf lembaga** dengan keterampilan digital dasar sehingga mereka mampu mengelola data secara mandiri, aman, dan terstruktur.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
Pelatihan dilaksanakan selama **dua hari** dengan pendekatan **workshop interaktif**. Tahapannya meliputi:

• **Sosialisasi konsep Big Data**: Analogi sederhana menggunakan data donasi harian, jumlah anak asuh, dan laporan keuangan.
• **Identifikasi kebutuhan data**: Diskusi dengan pengurus untuk memetakan entitas penting (anak yatim, donatur, program, transaksi).
• **Pembuatan database di NocoDB**: Peserta diajak membuat project, mengimpor data Excel, mendesain relasi tabel, dan mengatur hak akses pengguna.
• **Pengembangan antarmuka**: Membuat form input, dashboard ringkasan, dan laporan PDF otomatis.
• **Deployment lokal**: Aplikasi dihosting di server komunitas menggunakan Docker untuk akses internal.

Materi disusun dalam bahasa Indonesia dengan studi kasus nyata dari lembaga tersebut. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui **pre-test, post-test, dan kuesioner kepuasan**.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Pelatihan diikuti oleh **18 pengurus dan relawan** dengan latar belakang non-teknis. Hasilnya menunjukkan:

✅ **Peningkatan pemahaman konsep Big Data**: Skor rata-rata post-test naik dari 42% menjadi 89%.
✅ **Aplikasi database fungsional**: Sistem terdiri dari 5 tabel utama (anak, donatur, donasi, program, pengeluaran) dengan fitur pencarian dan ekspor.
✅ **Kepuasan peserta**: **97%** menyatakan pelatihan "sangat bermanfaat" dan "mudah diikuti".

Dalam 3 bulan pasca-pelatihan, lembaga telah **menghentikan penggunaan buku catatan fisik** dan beralih sepenuhnya ke sistem digital. Donatur juga melaporkan peningkatan kepercayaan karena transparansi laporan yang lebih cepat dan akurat.

Studi ini menjadi model replikabel untuk **pemberdayaan digital lembaga sosial berbasis komunitas**.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content:
Pengenalan teknologi Big Data dan tools low-code seperti **NocoDB** terbukti efektif dalam **meningkatkan kapasitas digital lembaga sosial non-profit**. Pendekatan tanpa coding menghilangkan hambatan teknis dan memungkinkan adopsi cepat oleh pengguna awam.

Kegiatan ini tidak hanya meningkatkan efisiensi operasional, tetapi juga memperkuat **tata kelola organisasi** dan **kepercayaan publik**. Rekomendasi ke depan:

• Pengembangan modul pelatihan berbasis video untuk skala nasional.
• Integrasi dengan sistem pembayaran digital (e.g., QRIS) untuk donasi real-time.
• Pelatihan lanjutan tentang visualisasi data menggunakan Metabase atau Power BI.

Digitalisasi lembaga sosial adalah langkah strategis menuju **masyarakat inklusif dan berkelanjutan**.

title: Enhancing IoT Data Acquisition Efficiency via FPGA-based Implementation with OpenCL Framework
author: Iman Firmansyah, Bambang Setiadi, Agus Subekti, Heri Nugraha, Edi Kurniawan, Yoshiki Yamaguchi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
The exponential growth of **Internet of Things (IoT)** devices has led to massive data streams requiring **low-latency, high-throughput processing** at the edge. Traditional microcontroller-based acquisition systems often suffer from **bottlenecks in real-time data handling**, especially when dealing with multi-sensor fusion or high-frequency sampling.

To overcome these limitations, this research proposes an **FPGA-based IoT data acquisition architecture** leveraging the **OpenCL (Open Computing Language) framework**. FPGAs offer **massive parallelism** and **reconfigurable hardware**, while OpenCL enables **high-level programming** of heterogeneous systems—combining the flexibility of software with the speed of hardware acceleration.

This approach is particularly relevant for applications such as **industrial monitoring, smart grids, and autonomous systems**, where microseconds matter and energy efficiency is critical.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
The system was implemented on an **Intel Cyclone V SoC FPGA**, which integrates dual ARM Cortex-A9 cores with programmable logic. The workflow includes:

• **Sensor interfacing**: Simultaneous acquisition from 8 analog sensors (0–5V, 1 MSPS) via high-speed ADCs.
• **OpenCL kernel design**: Custom kernels for **data filtering (FIR)**, **compression (delta encoding)**, and **timestamp synchronization**.
• **Host-device communication**: ARM processor runs Linux and manages data flow via PCIe-like Avalon interface.
• **Memory optimization**: Use of on-chip BRAM and DDR3 for zero-copy data transfer.
• **Benchmarking**: Compared against equivalent implementations on Raspberry Pi 4 and ESP32.

Development used **Intel FPGA SDK for OpenCL**, with kernels written in C99. Power consumption was measured using a precision multimeter, and latency was captured via logic analyzer.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
The FPGA-OpenCL system demonstrated significant performance gains:

✅ **Throughput**: **4.8× higher** than Raspberry Pi 4 (12.3 MB/s vs. 2.56 MB/s).
✅ **Latency**: End-to-end acquisition-to-output delay reduced to **<150 µs** (vs. 2.1 ms on ESP32).
✅ **Power efficiency**: **3.2× more efficient** (Joules per MB) than CPU-based systems.

The OpenCL framework reduced development time by **~60%** compared to traditional HDL (Verilog/VHDL), while maintaining **>95% of hardware-level performance**. Real-world testing in a factory environment showed **99.98% data integrity** under EMI noise.

Notably, the system supported **dynamic reconfiguration**—switching between sensor modes without reboot—enabling adaptive IoT deployments.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content:
This work validates **FPGA + OpenCL** as a compelling paradigm for **high-efficiency IoT data acquisition**. By abstracting hardware complexity, OpenCL democratizes FPGA programming for embedded developers while unlocking real-time performance unattainable with conventional processors.

The architecture is scalable to **dozens of sensors** and compatible with **edge AI inference** pipelines. Future directions include:

• Integration with **TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers** for on-device analytics.
• Support for **time-sensitive networking (TSN)** protocols.
• Exploration of **RISC-V soft-core + FPGA** hybrid designs.

As IoT systems grow in complexity, **hardware-accelerated, software-defined acquisition** will be essential for next-generation intelligent edge devices.

title: Penerapan Artificial Intelligence untuk Meningkatkan Efisiensi Pengelolaan Database Administrasi Remaja Masjid
author: Muhammad Bagus Andra, Eni Heni Hermaliani, Agus Subekti, Muhammad Haris

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Organisasi remaja masjid sering menghadapi tantangan dalam pengelolaan data administratif seperti keanggotaan, kehadiran, inventaris, dan laporan keuangan. Proses manual atau berbasis spreadsheet rentan terhadap kesalahan, lambat, dan kurang transparan. Dengan kemajuan teknologi, penerapan **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** menawarkan solusi inovatif untuk mengotomatisasi dan meningkatkan kualitas manajemen data di tingkat komunitas. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengintegrasikan AI ke dalam sistem administrasi remaja masjid sebagai bentuk penguatan literasi digital dan efisiensi operasional organisasi keagamaan.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
Sistem dikembangkan menggunakan pendekatan rekayasa perangkat lunak berbasis AI dengan komponen utama sebagai berikut:

• **Chatbot berbasis NLP** untuk menerima permintaan informasi dari anggota (misalnya: "Siapa yang hadir di acara kajian minggu lalu?").
• **Database relasional cerdas** yang dilengkapi modul deteksi duplikasi dan imputasi data otomatis.
• **Modul prediksi partisipasi** menggunakan algoritma *Random Forest* untuk memperkirakan kehadiran anggota berdasarkan riwayat aktivitas dan preferensi.
• Antarmuka web responsif untuk akses admin dan anggota.

Pengujian dilakukan melalui studi kasus di tiga remaja masjid di wilayah Jabodetabek selama periode tiga bulan, dengan metrik evaluasi berupa waktu pemrosesan data, akurasi entri, dan kepuasan pengguna.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Implementasi sistem menunjukkan hasil signifikan:

✅ **Pengurangan waktu administrasi** hingga 62% dibandingkan metode manual.
✅ **Akurasi pencatatan kehadiran** meningkat dari 84% menjadi 98%.
✅ **Tingkat kepuasan pengguna** mencapai 4.6 dari skala 5.

Chatbot mampu menjawab 92% pertanyaan umum tanpa intervensi manusia, sementara modul prediksi partisipasi mencapai akurasi 87% dalam memperkirakan kehadiran mingguan. Sistem juga berhasil mengurangi duplikasi data anggota hingga 100% melalui mekanisme validasi berbasis NIK dan nomor telepon.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Integrasi AI dalam administrasi remaja masjid terbukti efektif dalam meningkatkan efisiensi, akurasi, dan transparansi. Pendekatan ini tidak hanya memperkuat tata kelola organisasi komunitas, tetapi juga menjadi langkah awal pemberdayaan digital di lingkungan keagamaan. Ke depan, sistem dapat dikembangkan lebih lanjut dengan integrasi notifikasi otomatis, pelaporan keuangan berbasis AI, dan koneksi ke platform donasi digital. Model ini berpotensi direplikasi di berbagai organisasi kemasyarakatan lainnya sebagai bagian dari transformasi digital berbasis nilai lokal.

title: Multi View Natural Network for Cross-Project Software Defect Prediction
author: Boy Setiawan, Agus Subekti

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: **Cross-Project Software Defect Prediction (CPDP)** merupakan tantangan utama dalam *software quality assurance*, di mana model yang dilatih pada satu proyek gagal memberikan prediksi akurat pada proyek target karena perbedaan distribusi fitur dan konteks pengembangan. Masalah ini diperparah oleh **ketidakseimbangan kelas** (jumlah modul cacat jauh lebih sedikit daripada yang bersih) dan **heterogenitas metrik** antar proyek. Penelitian ini mengusulkan **Multi-View Neural Network (MVNN)** sebagai solusi arsitektural yang mampu menyelaraskan representasi lintas domain dan meningkatkan generalisasi model CPDP.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
MVNN dirancang dengan tiga komponen utama:

• **Multi-view encoder**: memproses input dari berbagai sumber fitur (misalnya: metrik kode statis, histori commit Git, dan struktur dependensi modul) melalui jalur jaringan saraf terpisah.
• **Feature alignment layer**: menggunakan *adversarial domain adaptation* dan *contrastive learning* untuk menyelaraskan representasi fitur ke dalam ruang embedding bersama.
• **Re-weighted classification head**: menerapkan *focal loss* dan *class-balanced sampling* untuk mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas.

Evaluasi dilakukan pada 12 proyek open-source dari repositori PROMISE, dengan skenario leave-one-project-out (LOPO). Performa dibandingkan terhadap baseline seperti **Transfer Component Analysis (TCA)**, **Deep Semantic Feature Learning (DSFL)**, dan **CODEP**.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
MVNN menunjukkan peningkatan konsisten dalam metrik evaluasi CPDP:

✅ **Rata-rata AUC**: 0.82 (naik 11% dibanding baseline terbaik).
✅ **F1-score**: 0.67 (naik 18% dibanding TCA).
✅ **G-mean**: 0.74, menunjukkan keseimbangan baik antara sensitivitas dan spesifisitas.

Analisis ablation menegaskan bahwa kontribusi terbesar berasal dari *feature alignment layer*, yang berhasil mengurangi *distribution shift* antar proyek hingga 34%. Selain itu, MVNN menunjukkan stabilitas tinggi bahkan pada proyek target dengan ukuran data sangat kecil (<50 modul).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Arsitektur **Multi-View Neural Network (MVNN)** terbukti efektif dalam mengatasi tantangan utama CPDP, yaitu perbedaan distribusi lintas proyek dan ketidakseimbangan kelas. Dengan memanfaatkan representasi multi-sumber dan mekanisme penyelarasan domain, MVNN memberikan generalisasi yang lebih baik dibanding pendekatan state-of-the-art. Penelitian ini membuka jalan bagi penerapan *deep transfer learning* yang lebih adaptif dalam *software engineering*. Ke depan, MVNN dapat diperluas untuk memprediksi jenis cacat tertentu atau diintegrasikan ke dalam pipeline CI/CD sebagai alat deteksi dini.

title: Leveraging 3GPP Features and Optimization Techniques for 5G NR-V2X Resource Allocation: A Survey
author: Chaeriah Bin Ali Wael, El Hadj Dogheche, Nasrullah Armi, Agus Subekti, Iyad Dayoub

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: **5G New Radio Vehicle-to-Everything (NR-V2X)** merupakan pilar kunci dalam pengembangan sistem transportasi cerdas (*Intelligent Transportation Systems / ITS*). NR-V2X memungkinkan komunikasi real-time antara kendaraan, infrastruktur, pejalan kaki, dan jaringan seluler untuk meningkatkan keselamatan dan efisiensi lalu lintas. Namun, alokasi sumber daya radio dalam lingkungan kendaraan yang sangat dinamis menghadirkan tantangan besar terkait **latensi ultra-rendah**, **keandalan tinggi**, dan **kebutuhan Quality of Service (QoS)** yang bervariasi. Penelitian ini menyajikan survei komprehensif terhadap fitur-fitur terbaru dari standar **3GPP Release 16 dan 17**, serta teknik optimisasi mutakhir untuk alokasi sumber daya NR-V2X.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
Studi ini menggunakan pendekatan *systematic literature review* (SLR) dengan cakupan publikasi dari tahun 2019 hingga 2023. Kriteria inklusi mencakup: (1) fokus pada NR-V2X (bukan LTE-V2X), (2) pembahasan eksplisit tentang alokasi sumber daya, dan (3) relevansi terhadap standar 3GPP. Sebanyak 78 makalah akademik dan dokumen teknis 3GPP dianalisis secara tematik.

Fitur 3GPP yang dikaji meliputi:
• **Mode sidelink terkoordinasi** (Mode 2 dengan grant dari gNodeB),
• **Resource reservation and reselection**,
• **QoS mapping untuk layanan V2X**,
• **Beam management untuk mobilitas tinggi**.

Teknik optimisasi yang dievaluasi mencakup pendekatan berbasis **game theory**, **reinforcement learning**, **graph neural networks**, dan **heuristic scheduling**.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Temuan utama menunjukkan bahwa integrasi fitur 3GPP terkini—khususnya **grant-based sidelink scheduling** dan **QoS-aware resource pools**—secara signifikan meningkatkan efisiensi spektrum dan keandalan komunikasi. Di sisi lain, teknik optimisasi berbasis **deep reinforcement learning (DRL)** menunjukkan performa terbaik dalam skenario lalu lintas padat, dengan:

✅ **Penurunan latensi rata-rata** hingga 38% dibanding metode statis,
✅ **Peningkatan delivery ratio** hingga 92% pada kecepatan kendaraan >100 km/jam,
✅ Kemampuan adaptif terhadap perubahan topologi jaringan dalam waktu <10 ms.

Namun, tantangan tetap ada terkait kompleksitas komputasi DRL dan interoperabilitas antar vendor.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Survei ini menegaskan bahwa sinergi antara **fitur standar 3GPP** dan **teknik optimisasi berbasis AI/ML** merupakan kunci keberhasilan alokasi sumber daya NR-V2X. Untuk masa depan, penelitian perlu fokus pada: (1) pengembangan framework alokasi sumber daya yang ringan (*lightweight*) untuk perangkat onboard, (2) integrasi dengan arsitektur jaringan terpadu 5G-Advanced, dan (3) validasi skala besar melalui uji coba lapangan. Hasil ini memberikan panduan strategis bagi insinyur standar, pengembang sistem, dan regulator dalam mewujudkan ekosistem V2X yang andal dan skalabel.

title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence into Radio Access Network (AI-RAN): Architecture, Classification, and Development Focus
author: Kirso Kirso, Agus Subekti

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Seiring evolusi jaringan nirkabel menuju **6G**, integrasi **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** ke dalam **Radio Access Network (RAN)** menjadi tak terhindarkan. AI-RAN tidak hanya meningkatkan efisiensi operasional, tetapi juga memungkinkan layanan yang lebih adaptif, responsif, dan aman. Namun, terminologi dan pendekatan AI-RAN masih sering tumpang tindih. Penelitian ini mengusulkan klasifikasi sistematis AI-RAN menjadi tiga paradigma utama: **AI-for-RAN**, **AI-and-RAN**, dan **AI-on-RAN**, serta mengidentifikasi fokus pengembangan strategis untuk dekade mendatang.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan analitis-komparatif terhadap 60+ studi terkini (2020–2024) dari jurnal IEEE, 3GPP, dan konferensi utama seperti ICC dan Globecom. Ketiga paradigma AI-RAN didefinisikan sebagai berikut:

• **AI-for-RAN**: AI digunakan sebagai alat eksternal untuk mengoptimalkan fungsi RAN (misalnya: prediksi beban jaringan).
• **AI-and-RAN**: AI dan RAN dikembangkan secara paralel dengan interaksi dua arah (misalnya: RAN menyediakan data pelatihan untuk model AI).
• **AI-on-RAN**: AI di-*embed* langsung ke dalam fungsi RAN (misalnya: *AI-native baseband processing*).

Setiap paradigma dievaluasi berdasarkan kedalaman integrasi, overhead komputasi, latensi inferensi, dan kesiapan implementasi.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Klasifikasi ini mengungkap tren dominan:

✅ **AI-for-RAN** paling matang dan banyak diadopsi di jaringan 5G komersial saat ini (contoh: *AI-driven beamforming*).
✅ **AI-and-RAN** menunjukkan potensi besar dalam *network slicing* dan *dynamic spectrum sharing*.
✅ **AI-on-RAN** masih dalam tahap riset awal, tetapi menjadi fondasi utama untuk **6G RAN**.

Fokus pengembangan utama yang teridentifikasi meliputi:
• **Efisiensi spektrum** melalui *semantic communication*,
• **Latensi ultra-rendah** (<1 ms) dengan *in-RAN inference*,
• **Keamanan jaringan** berbasis *anomaly detection* berbasis federated learning,
• **Sustainability** melalui *AI-powered energy saving* di base station.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Kerangka klasifikasi AI-RAN yang diusulkan memberikan pemahaman yang lebih jelas tentang tingkat integrasi AI dalam jaringan akses radio. Setiap paradigma memiliki peran strategis: AI-for-RAN untuk transisi jangka pendek, AI-and-RAN untuk evolusi 5G-Advanced, dan AI-on-RAN sebagai tulang punggung 6G. Tantangan utama ke depan meliputi standardisasi antarmuka AI-RAN, manajemen privasi data, dan desain chip khusus (*AI accelerators*) untuk perangkat RAN. Penelitian ini menjadi panduan bagi akademisi dan industri dalam merancang arsitektur jaringan nirkabel generasi berikutnya yang benar-benar cerdas.

title: Ensemble And Voting Approaches For Defect Prediction Across Multiple Software Projects
author: Kirso Kirso, Agus Subekti

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Prediksi cacat perangkat lunak lintas proyek (*Cross-Project Defect Prediction / CPDP*) tetap menjadi tantangan utama karena perbedaan distribusi fitur dan ketidakseimbangan kelas antar proyek. Pendekatan berbasis model tunggal sering gagal menggeneralisasi ke proyek target yang berbeda secara signifikan. Penelitian ini mengeksplorasi pemanfaatan **metode ensemble dan voting** dari lima algoritma machine learning untuk meningkatkan stabilitas dan akurasi prediksi CPDP, terutama dalam skenario di mana proyek sumber dan target memiliki pola struktural yang serupa.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
Lima model dasar dipilih berdasarkan keragaman arsitektur dan performa historis: **Logistic Regression**, **Random Forest**, **XGBoost**, **Support Vector Machine (SVM)**, dan **k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN)**. Ketiganya digabungkan menggunakan tiga skema voting:

• **Hard Voting**: mayoritas keputusan kelas,
• **Soft Voting**: rata-rata probabilitas prediksi,
• **Weighted Voting**: bobot berdasarkan performa validasi silang di proyek sumber.

Evaluasi dilakukan pada 10 proyek open-source dari repositori PROMISE menggunakan skenario *leave-one-project-out*. Metrik utama meliputi **F1-score**, **AUC**, dan **Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)** untuk menangani ketidakseimbangan kelas.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Hasil menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan ensemble memberikan peningkatan signifikan ketika proyek sumber dan target memiliki kemiripan struktural (misalnya: proyek Java berbasis GUI):

✅ **Rata-rata F1-score**: 0.71 (naik 14% dibanding model terbaik tunggal),
✅ **Stabilitas prediksi** meningkat, dengan deviasi standar F1 turun 22%.

Namun, kinerja menurun tajam (F1 < 0.45) saat proyek target sangat berbeda (misalnya: sistem embedded vs aplikasi web), mengonfirmasi bahwa **perbedaan distribusi data** tetap menjadi hambatan utama CPDP. Skema *soft voting* konsisten menjadi yang terbaik di sebagian besar kasus.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Metode ensemble dan voting terbukti efektif dalam meningkatkan kinerja CPDP pada pasangan proyek yang memiliki kesamaan domain atau arsitektur. Namun, hasil ini juga menegaskan bahwa tanpa mekanisme adaptasi domain yang kuat, ensemble saja tidak cukup untuk mengatasi *distribution shift* yang ekstrem. Penelitian lanjutan direkomendasikan untuk menggabungkan ensemble dengan teknik *transfer learning* atau *feature alignment*, sehingga menciptakan sistem CPDP yang lebih tangguh dan universal.

title: Macro-Level Energy Demand Model for Cellular Telecommunication Networks
author: Mochamad Mardi Marta Dinata, Yohei Yamaguchi, Hideaki Uchida, Yoshiyuki Shimoda, Agus Subekti

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Konsumsi energi jaringan telekomunikasi seluler terus meningkat seiring dengan ekspansi 4G/5G dan kepadatan pengguna. Perencanaan infrastruktur yang efisien memerlukan pemahaman kuantitatif tentang **kebutuhan energi makro** di tingkat kota atau regional. Namun, sebagian besar model saat ini bersifat mikro (per base station) atau tidak mempertimbangkan komposisi heterogen infrastruktur. Penelitian ini mengembangkan kerangka pemodelan energi makro berbasis **komposisi dan tipe Base Transceiver Station (BTS)** untuk mendukung perencanaan jaringan yang berkelanjutan.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
Model dikembangkan menggunakan data nyata dari tiga kota besar di Indonesia, mencakup lebih dari 12.000 BTS dari berbagai generasi (2G hingga 5G) dan vendor (Ericsson, Huawei, Nokia). Setiap tipe BTS dikategorikan berdasarkan:

• Teknologi akses (GSM, UMTS, LTE, NR),
• Konfigurasi daya (single/dual/triple band),
• Tipe situs (macro, micro, indoor).

Konsumsi energi per tipe diukur melalui audit lapangan dan data vendor. Model akhir dirumuskan sebagai:

**E_total = Σ (N_i × P_i × U_i)**

Di mana:
- *N_i* = jumlah BTS tipe *i*,
- *P_i* = daya rata-rata (kW),
- *U_i* = faktor utilitas berbasis beban lalu lintas.

Validasi dilakukan dengan membandingkan prediksi model terhadap tagihan listrik bulanan operator.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Model menunjukkan akurasi tinggi dalam memprediksi konsumsi energi makro:

✅ **Kesalahan rata-rata absolut (MAPE)**: 6.3%,
✅ **Korelasi (R²)**: 0.94 terhadap data aktual.

Analisis sensitivitas mengungkap bahwa **komposisi tipe BTS** berkontribusi 68% terhadap variasi total energi, sementara kepadatan pengguna hanya 22%. Model juga berhasil memprediksi penghematan energi hingga **18%** melalui strategi seperti *site consolidation* dan migrasi ke perangkat generasi terbaru.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Kerangka pemodelan energi makro ini memberikan alat praktis bagi operator seluler dan regulator dalam merancang kebijakan efisiensi energi, perencanaan kapasitas, dan transisi ke infrastruktur hijau. Model bersifat skalabel, dapat diterapkan di berbagai wilayah dengan kalibrasi minimal, dan mendukung simulasi skenario seperti densifikasi 5G atau penutupan jaringan 2G/3G. Ke depan, integrasi dengan data geospasial dan prediksi pertumbuhan pengguna akan semakin memperkuat utilitas model ini dalam perencanaan jangka panjang.

title: A LIGHTWEIGHT AND PRACTICAL PIPELINE FOR CROSS-PROJECT DEFECT PREDICTION USING METRIC-BASED LEARNING
author: Novia Heriyani, Agus Subekti

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Meskipun model *deep learning* menunjukkan performa tinggi dalam *Cross-Project Defect Prediction* (CPDP), kompleksitas komputasi dan kebutuhan data besar membuatnya kurang praktis untuk diadopsi di banyak organisasi pengembang perangkat lunak. Penelitian ini mengusulkan **pipeline CPDP ringan dan praktis** yang memanfaatkan fitur metrik tradisional (seperti LOC, cyclomatic complexity, dan coupling) dikombinasikan dengan teknik adaptasi domain dan penanganan ketidakseimbangan kelas, menggunakan algoritma LightGBM sebagai inti prediksi.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content:
Pipeline terdiri dari tiga tahap utama:

1. **Preprocessing**: Pembersihan data dan normalisasi fitur metrik statis.
2. **Domain Adaptation**: Transformasi fitur menggunakan **TCA (Transfer Component Analysis)** dan varian **TCA+** untuk menyelaraskan distribusi proyek sumber dan target.
3. **Resampling & Prediksi**: Penanganan ketidakseimbangan kelas dengan **SMOTEENN**, diikuti oleh pelatihan model **LightGBM**—algoritma boosting berbasis pohon yang efisien secara memori dan cepat.

Evaluasi dilakukan pada 14 proyek dari repositori PROMISE dan AEEEM dengan skenario *leave-one-project-out*. Performa dibandingkan terhadap baseline seperti DeepCPDP, CODEP, dan TCA+ dengan SVM.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content:
Pipeline yang diusulkan menunjukkan keseimbangan optimal antara performa dan efisiensi:

✅ **Rata-rata F1-score**: 0.69 — setara dengan model deep learning terbaik,
✅ **Waktu pelatihan rata-rata**: <3 detik per proyek (vs >120 detik untuk model deep learning),
✅ **Penggunaan memori**: <200 MB.

Stabilitas model juga tinggi, dengan deviasi F1 hanya ±0.05 di berbagai pasangan proyek. Hasil ini membuktikan bahwa pendekatan berbasis metrik tradisional, bila dikombinasikan dengan teknik transfer learning yang tepat, tetap sangat kompetitif bahkan di era AI.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Pipeline CPDP ringan ini menawarkan solusi realistis dan siap pakai bagi tim pengembang perangkat lunak yang ingin menerapkan prediksi cacat lintas proyek tanpa infrastruktur AI yang mahal. Dengan memanfaatkan fitur yang mudah diekstraksi dan algoritma yang efisien, pendekatan ini menjembatani kesenjangan antara riset akademis dan praktik industri. Untuk pengembangan lebih lanjut, pipeline dapat diperluas dengan integrasi fitur dinamis (misalnya: histori commit) dan antarmuka berbasis web untuk adopsi yang lebih luas.

title: INDUSTRIAL INTERNET OF THINGS: RECENT ADVANCES, ENABLING TECHNOLOGIES AND OPEN CHALLENGES
author: Wazir Zada Khan, MH Rehman, Hussein Mohammed Zangoti, Muhammad Khalil Afzal, Nasrullah Armi, Khaled Salah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) represents a transformative evolution of IoT in industrial environments, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and intelligent automation. Unlike consumer IoT, IIoT demands ultra-reliable communication, low latency, and seamless integration with legacy industrial systems. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of IIoT, clarifying its definition, core architecture, and distinguishing it from conventional IoT through its focus on operational efficiency, asset optimization, and process intelligence in manufacturing and critical infrastructure.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The study adopts a systematic literature review approach, analyzing over 120 peer-reviewed publications from 2015–2019. Key IIoT components are categorized into: (1) sensing and actuation layers, (2) communication protocols (e.g., MQTT, OPC UA, 5G TSN), (3) edge and cloud computing frameworks, and (4) AI-driven analytics for decision-making. The authors also map enabling technologies such as digital twins, fog computing, and blockchain for security, while identifying gaps in standardization and interoperability.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The analysis reveals that IIoT adoption is accelerating in smart manufacturing, energy, and logistics, with 68% of recent deployments leveraging edge AI for real-time anomaly detection. However, major challenges persist: (1) lack of unified security frameworks across OT/IT boundaries, (2) scalability issues in heterogeneous device ecosystems, and (3) insufficient QoS guarantees in wireless industrial networks. The paper highlights that only 22% of surveyed systems implement end-to-end encryption, exposing critical infrastructure to cyber-physical threats.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: While IIoT offers unprecedented opportunities for industrial digitization, its full potential remains constrained by fragmented standards and security vulnerabilities. The authors advocate for cross-industry collaboration to develop modular, secure-by-design IIoT architectures. Future work should focus on lightweight cryptographic protocols for resource-constrained devices and AI-native platforms that unify data from legacy SCADA systems with modern sensor networks.

title: ERROR RATE DETECTION DUE TO PRIMARY USER EMULATION ATTACK IN COGNITIVE RADIO NETWORKS
author: Nasrullah Armi, W Gharibi, Wazir Zada Khan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs) rely on accurate spectrum sensing to detect Primary User (PU) signals and enable dynamic spectrum access. However, Primary User Emulation Attacks (PUEA) pose a severe threat by spoofing PU signals, leading to false spectrum occupancy reports and denial-of-service for legitimate Secondary Users (SUs). This paper investigates the impact of PUEA in spatially constrained environments and evaluates detection performance under varying attack radii.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The authors model a CRN with a single PU, multiple SUs, and a malicious PUEA node. Two exclusive protection zones around the PU are defined: 30m and 50m, within which attackers are prohibited. Energy detection is used as the sensing mechanism. The system evaluates two key metrics: Probability of False Alarm (Pf) — when SUs incorrectly detect PU presence — and Probability of Miss Detection (Pm) — when PU signals are missed. Simulations are conducted using MATLAB under AWGN channel conditions with varying signal-to-noise ratios (SNR).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Results demonstrate that expanding the exclusive zone from 30m to 50m reduces Pf by 37% and Pm by 29% at SNR = -10 dB. At higher SNR (-5 dB), the 50m zone achieves Pf < 0.05 and Pm < 0.1, indicating robust detection resilience. The study confirms that spatial isolation of legitimate PUs significantly mitigates PUEA effectiveness, as attackers farther from the PU produce weaker, less convincing emulated signals.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Enforcing larger exclusive zones around primary transmitters is a practical, low-overhead countermeasure against PUEA. While not eliminating the threat entirely, this spatial strategy substantially improves detection reliability without requiring complex cryptographic or cooperative sensing mechanisms. Future work will explore hybrid approaches combining spatial constraints with machine learning-based anomaly detection for enhanced security.

title: EXPERIMENTAL CHARACTERIZATION OF AMC-BASED THIN TUNABLE ABSORBER USING VARACTOR DIODE
author: Muthia Hanifah, Levy Olivia Nur, Nasrullah Armi, Ivany Sarief, Achmad Munir

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Electromagnetic absorbers are critical in reducing interference and enhancing signal integrity in modern wireless systems. This work presents a thin, tunable absorber based on Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) technology, designed for dynamic frequency adjustment in the S-band. The tunability is achieved by integrating varactor diodes, enabling real-time reconfiguration without mechanical changes.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The absorber consists of a 2×2 AMC unit cell array printed on a 1.6mm FR4 substrate (104mm × 104mm). Each unit cell incorporates a varactor diode controlled by a reverse DC bias voltage (0–15V). A 470Ω resistor is added in parallel to each diode to improve impedance matching and absorption bandwidth. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations are performed using CST Studio Suite, followed by experimental validation using a horn antenna setup in an anechoic chamber.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The prototype achieves continuous frequency tuning from 2.26 GHz to 2.68 GHz as the bias voltage increases from 0V to 15V. At 2.45 GHz (ISM band), a peak absorptivity of 98.5% (reflection coefficient S11 = -18.2 dB) is recorded. The addition of the 470Ω resistor broadens the -10 dB bandwidth by 120 MHz compared to the resistor-less design. Experimental results align closely with simulations, confirming the design’s reliability and tunability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: This AMC-based tunable absorber offers a compact, low-cost solution for adaptive electromagnetic shielding in 5G, radar, and IoT applications. Its voltage-controlled tuning mechanism eliminates the need for physical reconfiguration, making it ideal for dynamic RF environments. Future enhancements include integration with microcontroller-based bias control for autonomous frequency tracking.

title: QOS PERFORMANCE OF SOFTWARE DEFINED NETWORK USING OPEN NETWORK OPERATING SYSTEM CONTROLLER
author: Rafli Ramadhan, Nasrullah Armi, Rita Magdalena, Galih Nugraha Nurkahfi, Mochamad Mardi Marta Dinata

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) decouples the control and data planes, enabling centralized network management and programmability. This paper evaluates the Quality of Service (QoS) performance of SDN using the Open Network Operating System (ONOS) controller, focusing on key metrics such as throughput, delay, jitter, and packet loss in virtualized network topologies.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A testbed is built using Mininet to emulate 20 hosts and 10 OpenFlow switches under two topologies: linear and ring. ONOS serves as the SDN controller, managing flow rules and network state. Traffic is generated using iperf3, and QoS metrics are measured over 100 iterations. The experiment compares performance under identical load conditions to isolate topology effects on network behavior.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The linear topology achieves: throughput = 4.9 kbps, delay = 2.69 ms, jitter = 0.7 μs, and packet loss = 1.4%. In contrast, the ring topology shows superior performance: throughput = 8.2 kbps (+67%), delay = 1.85 ms (-31%), jitter = 0.4 μs (-43%), and packet loss = 0.6% (-57%). The ring’s redundancy and multiple paths reduce congestion and improve fault tolerance, validating its suitability for mission-critical applications.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: ONOS demonstrates robust QoS management in SDN environments, with topology choice significantly impacting performance. Ring topologies are recommended for high-availability services, while linear topologies may suffice for simpler, cost-sensitive deployments. Future work will integrate machine learning into ONOS for predictive traffic engineering and dynamic topology optimization.

title: DESIGN AND CHARACTERIZATION OF 1800MHZ TM MODE CIRCULAR WAVEGUIDE ARRAY ANTENNA FOR ENERGY HARVESTING APPLICATION
author: Muhammad Panji Kusuma Praja, Winy Desvasari, Nasrullah Armi, Achmad Munir

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Ambient RF energy harvesting offers a sustainable power source for low-power IoT devices. This research focuses on designing a 2×2 circular waveguide array antenna operating at 1800 MHz (GSM band) in Transverse Magnetic (TM) mode to maximize energy capture from cellular base stations. The asymmetric configuration aims to enhance gain and bandwidth while maintaining compactness.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Each waveguide element is designed with a radius of 68mm and height of 40mm to resonate at 1800 MHz. The array is fed via a microstrip line network optimized through parametric simulation in HFSS. A prototype is fabricated on FR4 substrate with total dimensions of 350mm × 350mm. Performance is characterized using a vector network analyzer (VNA) to measure reflection coefficient (S11) and radiation patterns in an anechoic chamber.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The fabricated array achieves an excellent impedance match with S11 = -30.32 dB at 1800 MHz, indicating over 99.9% power absorption. The asymmetric layout yields a measured gain of 8.7 dBi and a 3-dB bandwidth of 45 MHz. Far-field measurements confirm a directional radiation pattern suitable for focused energy harvesting in urban environments with strong GSM signals.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The proposed TM-mode circular waveguide array is a highly efficient solution for GSM-band energy harvesting, combining high gain, deep impedance matching, and structural simplicity. Its performance surpasses conventional patch and dipole harvesters in the same band. Future work will integrate this antenna with a rectenna circuit to demonstrate full RF-to-DC conversion for powering wireless sensors.

title: PATH LOSS MODEL OF THE MARITIME WIRELESS COMMUNICATION IN THE SEAS OF INDONESIA
author: Arumjeni Mitayani, Galih Nugraha Nurkahfi, Mochamad Mardi Marta Dinata, Vita Awalia Mardiana, Nasrullah Armi, Chaeriah Bin Ali Wael, Arief Suryadi Satyawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Maritime wireless communication is essential for supporting surveillance, fisheries, and exploration activities across Indonesia’s vast archipelago. However, radio wave propagation over sea surfaces differs significantly from terrestrial environments due to dynamic sea conditions. This study investigates how sea state—classified using the Douglas Sea Scale—affects path loss and, consequently, the reliability of maritime wireless links.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The research models path loss under varying sea conditions, ranging from calm (Douglas Scale 1) to rough (Douglas Scale 6). Simulations are conducted using ray-tracing and two-ray ground reflection models, adjusted for sea surface roughness and wave height. Key parameters include transmitter-receiver distance (1–10 km), antenna height (5–20 m), and frequency (2.4 GHz). Performance metrics include signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and bit error rate (BER) under different sea states.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Results confirm a strong correlation between sea roughness and path loss severity. In calm seas (Scale 1–2), path loss follows standard two-ray model predictions. However, in rough seas (Scale 5–6), additional path loss of up to 12 dB is observed due to wave scattering and multipath fading. At 5 km distance, BER increases from 10⁻⁶ (calm) to 10⁻³ (rough), significantly degrading communication quality. The study proposes an empirical path loss correction factor based on real-time sea state data.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Accurate path loss modeling in Indonesian maritime environments must account for dynamic sea conditions. The proposed model enables more robust link budget planning for coastal and offshore communication systems. Future work includes integrating real-time oceanographic data into adaptive modulation schemes to maintain QoS under varying sea states.

title: A RELIABLE PUBLIC SAFETY FRAMEWORK FOR INDUSTRIAL INTERNET OF THINGS (IIOT)
author: Faheem Reegu, Wazir Zada Khan, Salwani Mohd Daud, Quratulain Arshad, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: As Industry 4.0 transforms manufacturing through IIoT, ensuring public safety (PS) becomes paramount—especially in high-risk sectors like oil and gas. Traditional safety systems are often siloed and reactive. This paper introduces IoTPS: an integrated, proactive Public Safety framework leveraging IIoT for real-time hazard detection, emergency response, and worker protection.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: IoTPS integrates heterogeneous sensors (gas, temperature, motion, wearable biometrics) with edge computing and cloud analytics. The architecture features three layers: (1) perception layer (sensors and actuators), (2) network layer (LPWAN/5G for data transmission), and (3) application layer (AI-driven risk prediction and alerting). A case study in an oil refinery validates the framework’s ability to detect gas leaks, fire outbreaks, and personnel distress.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: In the oil and gas case study, IoTPS reduced emergency response time by 68% compared to conventional systems. The framework achieved 99.2% detection accuracy for hazardous gas concentrations and enabled real-time evacuation routing via digital twins of the facility. System reliability was enhanced through redundant communication paths and blockchain-based incident logging for auditability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: IoTPS demonstrates that IIoT can significantly elevate public safety from reactive to predictive. Its modular design allows adaptation across industries—from chemical plants to smart cities. Future enhancements include drone-based emergency response integration and federated learning for cross-facility threat pattern recognition.

title: COOPERATIVE GAME THEORY APPROACH FOR ENERGY-EFFICIENT NODE CLUSTERING IN WIRELESS SENSOR NETWORK
author: Salita Ulitia Prini, Winy Desvasari, Rico Dahlan, Ros Sariningrum

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Energy efficiency is critical in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) due to the limited battery capacity of sensor nodes. Clustering is a proven technique to prolong network lifetime, but traditional methods like LEACH often suffer from uneven energy distribution. This paper proposes a Cooperative Game Theoretic Clustering (CGC) algorithm that models cluster formation as a cost-sharing game among nodes to optimize energy usage.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: CGC treats each potential cluster head as a player in a 3-agent cooperative game, where coalition formation minimizes total energy cost for data aggregation and transmission. The Shapley value is used to fairly distribute energy load among coalition members. Performance is evaluated via MATLAB simulations against LEACH in networks of 50–200 nodes, measuring: (1) network lifetime, (2) stability period (time until first/half nodes die), and (3) residual energy.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: CGC outperforms LEACH in small-to-medium networks (≤100 nodes): First Node Dies (FND) is delayed by 65%, and Half Node Dies (HND) by 52.4%. Total residual energy at HND is 38% higher in CGC. However, as node count exceeds 150, LEACH’s simplicity gives it a slight edge due to lower overhead. CGC’s strength lies in balanced energy consumption, reducing hotspots and extending operational stability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Cooperative game theory offers a mathematically sound approach to energy-aware clustering in WSNs. While CGC excels in moderate-scale deployments, hybrid strategies combining game theory with lightweight protocols may be optimal for large networks. Future work will explore dynamic coalition reformation based on real-time energy levels.

title: ANALISIS KINERJA LIGHT DETECTING AND RANGING (LIDAR) UNTUK DETEKSI OBJEK MENGGUNAKAN METODE JARAK EUCLIDEAN
author: Giovano Andara, Dharu Arseno, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Object detection in confined spaces requires high precision and reliability. Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) technology offers accurate 3D spatial mapping through point cloud data. This study evaluates the performance of a ground-based YDLiDAR G4 sensor for indoor object detection using Euclidean distance as the core metric for distinguishing objects from background.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Experiments are conducted in a 5.76m × 4.95m indoor room with two static objects placed at varying distances. The YDLiDAR G4 scans at 5 Hz and 12 Hz, generating 2D point cloud data (x, y coordinates). Euclidean distance is computed between consecutive points to segment objects: points with inter-distance below a threshold are grouped as a single object. Detection accuracy and processing latency are measured across scanning frequencies.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: At 12 Hz, the system achieves 94.7% object detection accuracy with an average latency of 83 ms, outperforming the 5 Hz mode (89.2% accuracy, 192 ms latency). Euclidean distance effectively isolates objects within 0.5–3.0 m range, with precision dropping beyond 3.5 m due to beam divergence. False positives are reduced by 40% using adaptive distance thresholds based on local point density.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Euclidean distance is a computationally efficient and effective method for object detection in indoor LiDAR applications. Higher scanning frequencies significantly improve real-time performance, making the YDLiDAR G4 suitable for robotics and smart environment monitoring. Future work will extend the method to 3D LiDAR and dynamic object tracking.

title: DESIGN AND REALIZATION OF BAND PASS FILTER IN K-BAND FREQUENCY FOR SHORT RANGE RADAR APPLICATION
author: Prasetyo Putranto, Nasrullah Armi, Dharu Arseno

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Short-Range Radar (SRR) systems operating in the K-band (24 GHz) require high-resolution sensing, necessitating wide bandwidths (~1 GHz). A critical component is the bandpass filter (BPF), which must pass the desired frequency while rejecting out-of-band interference. This paper presents the design and fabrication of a wideband BPF using Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology for SRR applications.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The BPF is designed on RO4003C substrate using SIW technique to achieve low loss and high power handling. The structure is optimized via electromagnetic simulation to center at 24 GHz with 1 GHz bandwidth. Key performance metrics—VSWR, return loss, insertion loss, and physical dimensions—are analyzed. A prototype is fabricated and measured using a vector network analyzer (VNA) to validate simulated results.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Simulation shows excellent performance: VSWR = 1.03, return loss = -36.93 dB, insertion loss = -0.67 dB. However, measurement reveals VSWR = 2.07, return loss = -8.14 dB, insertion loss = -4.32 dB, with bandwidth reduced by ~50%. The discrepancy is attributed to fabrication tolerances, connector mismatches, and substrate inhomogeneity—common challenges in millimeter-wave prototyping.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: While the SIW-based BPF achieves wide bandwidth in simulation, real-world performance is limited by manufacturing imperfections. Future work will focus on tighter fabrication control and alternative topologies (e.g., defected ground structures) to improve measured results. Despite limitations, the design provides a viable foundation for K-band SRR front-end systems.

title: A REVIEW OF THE USE CASES AND POSSIBLE TECHNOLOGIES FOR 5G AND BEYOND COMMUNICATIONS
author: Ali Mahamoud Ali, Bakhit Amine Adoum, Idriss Saleh Bachar, Nasrullah Armi, Mahamat Saleh Idriss, Mahamoud Youssouf Khayal

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: As 5G deployment accelerates globally, understanding its use cases and enabling technologies is crucial for stakeholders across industries. This paper provides a comprehensive review of 5G applications and the key technological enablers that support ultra-reliable, low-latency, and massive connectivity requirements.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The study conducts a systematic survey of 5G literature, categorizing use cases into three pillars: (1) enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB), (2) Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communications (URLLC), and (3) massive Machine-Type Communications (mMTC). For each, the paper analyzes enabling technologies: Massive MIMO, beamforming, NOMA, D2D, full duplex, small cells, and cognitive radio.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The analysis reveals that no single technology suffices; instead, 5G relies on synergistic integration. Massive MIMO boosts spectral efficiency but increases complexity. NOMA enhances user multiplexing yet suffers from error propagation. Full duplex doubles spectral efficiency but requires near-perfect self-interference cancellation. The paper maps each technology to specific use cases—e.g., URLLC for autonomous vehicles, mMTC for smart cities.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: 5G’s true potential lies in its heterogeneous technology stack, tailored to diverse verticals. Future 6G systems will build on this foundation with AI-native air interfaces and terahertz communications. Policymakers and engineers must collaborate to standardize and deploy these technologies responsibly.

title: IMPACT OF OVERLOADING FACTOR ON MIMO–SCMA SYSTEMS
author: Vita Awalia Mardiana, Dayat Kurniawan, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Sparse Code Multiple Access (SCMA) is a promising non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme for 5G, enabling massive connectivity by allowing multiple users to share the same time-frequency resource. When combined with MIMO, system capacity increases further—but at the cost of higher complexity. This paper investigates how overloading factor (user-to-resource ratio) affects MIMO-SCMA performance.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The study simulates SCMA and MIMO-SCMA systems under Rayleigh fading and AWGN channels, with overloading factors from 100% (1:1) to 300% (3:1). Performance is evaluated using Bit Error Rate (BER) and processing time. The MIMO configuration uses 2×2 antennas, and detection employs message-passing algorithm (MPA).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: As overloading increases to 300%, BER degrades for both systems, but MIMO-SCMA maintains superior BER performance due to spatial diversity. However, processing time rises exponentially—MIMO-SCMA takes 3.2× longer than single SCMA at 300% overload. At 200% overload, MIMO-SCMA achieves BER = 10⁻³ at 8 dB SNR, while single SCMA requires 12 dB.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: MIMO-SCMA offers significant BER gains in overloaded scenarios but suffers from high computational complexity. For delay-sensitive applications, a trade-off between overloading factor and processing capability is essential. Future work will explore deep learning-based detectors to reduce complexity.

title: COMPARATIVE STUDY OF THE LEACH AND LEACH-PSO PROTOCOLS ON WIRELESS SENSOR NETWORKS
author: Nasrullah Armi, Adira Nur Andiyani, Helfy Susilawati, Chaeriah Bin Ali Wael

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Energy efficiency is paramount in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) due to limited battery capacity. LEACH (Low-Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy) is a classic clustering protocol, but its random cluster head selection leads to uneven energy consumption. This paper compares LEACH with LEACH-PSO, which uses Particle Swarm Optimization to select optimal cluster heads.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Both protocols are simulated in MATLAB with 100 nodes over a 100m×100m area. Metrics include: (1) network lifetime (time until first/last node dies), (2) total energy consumption, and (3) number of alive nodes over time. LEACH-PSO uses PSO to minimize intra-cluster distance and balance energy load.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: LEACH-PSO extends network stability period by 22%—first node dies at round 1,240 vs. 1,015 in LEACH. Total network lifetime increases by 18%. However, LEACH-PSO causes earlier death of some edge nodes due to PSO’s focus on centroid optimization, leading to slightly uneven energy distribution in sparse regions.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LEACH-PSO improves overall energy efficiency and network longevity but may sacrifice edge-node fairness. Hybrid approaches combining PSO with residual energy weighting could mitigate this. The study confirms that intelligent cluster head selection significantly enhances WSN sustainability.

title: SIMONIC: IOT BASED QUARANTINE MONITORING SYSTEM FOR COVID-19
author: Vita Awalia Mardiana, Mochamad Mardi Martadinata, Galih Nugraha Nurkahfi, Arumjeni Mitayani, Dayat Kurniawan, Nasrullah Armi, Asih Setiarini

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: During the COVID-19 pandemic, effective quarantine enforcement and social distancing were critical. SIMONIC is an integrated IoT system that combines geofencing and proximity detection to monitor quarantine compliance and prevent close contact, offering a unified solution beyond single-function systems.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system uses a low-cost, reusable wristband (BLE-based) paired with an Android app. Geofencing leverages GPS and the Traccar platform to define quarantine zones. Social distancing uses RSSI-based distance estimation with adaptive thresholds. Optimal BLE advertising/scanning intervals are determined experimentally. Performance is evaluated via precision, recall, accuracy, and F-measure.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The optimal BLE interval is 7 seconds for both wristband and smartphone, balancing battery life and detection latency. Geofence accuracy reaches 92.3%, while social distancing achieves 88.7% F-measure at 1.5m threshold. False alarms are minimized through RSSI filtering and moving average calibration.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: SIMONIC demonstrates that an integrated, low-cost IoT system can effectively support public health measures during pandemics. Its modular design allows adaptation to other contact-tracing or asset-tracking scenarios. Future work includes integration with health authority dashboards for real-time monitoring.

title: PERANCANGAN MEDIA PEMBELAJARAN MODULASI DIGITAL (ASK, FSK, BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM) BERBASIS AUGMENTED REALITY
author: Riz-riz Rahmat Taufik, Ahmad Tri Hanuranto, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Understanding digital modulation (ASK, FSK, BPSK, etc.) is challenging for students due to its abstract nature. This project develops an Augmented Reality (AR) learning application that visualizes modulation waveforms in 3D when users scan physical markers, enhancing conceptual comprehension through interactive visualization.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The AR app is built using Unity3D and Vuforia SDK for Android. Modulation waveforms are designed in Adobe Illustrator and rendered as 3D objects. Users scan printed markers with their smartphone camera to trigger waveform displays. A UI button allows switching between bit sequences to show dynamic waveform changes. Usability is evaluated via Mean Opinion Score (MOS) surveys.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: All core functions work reliably. MOS scores are: 3.37 (appearance), 3.37 (functionality), and 3.45 (educational benefit)—indicating 'good' to 'very good' user satisfaction. Marker detection is stable up to 20 cm distance with adequate lighting. Students report improved understanding of phase and amplitude changes across modulation types.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The AR-based learning media effectively bridges theory and visualization in digital communications education. Its low-cost, marker-based approach makes it accessible for classrooms with limited lab equipment. Future versions will include interactive quizzes and real-time signal generation from microphone input.

title: IMPLEMENTASI SISTEM DETEKSI JARAK KENDARAAN MENGGUNAKAN SENSOR ULTRASONIK
author: Muhammad Ilham Aditya, Arsyad Ramadhan Darlis, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Traffic congestion increases rear-end collision risks, especially in stop-and-go conditions. This project implements a low-cost vehicle distance monitoring system using ultrasonic sensors to alert drivers of unsafe following distances, enhancing road safety in urban environments.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system uses an Arduino Uno microcontroller and HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor mounted on the rear of a vehicle. Distance is calculated from echo time. Three alert zones are defined: <30 cm (red LED + continuous buzzer), 30–120 cm (yellow LED + intermittent buzzer), >120 cm (green LED). An LCD displays real-time distance. The prototype is tested in static and slow-moving scenarios.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system accurately detects distances from 5 cm to 300 cm with ±2 cm error. Alert logic functions as designed: red zone triggers immediate warning, yellow provides caution, green indicates safety. Power consumption is low (120 mA), suitable for 12V automotive systems. Limitations include reduced accuracy in heavy rain or high wind.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: This ultrasonic-based system offers an affordable, real-time solution for collision avoidance in low-speed traffic. While not a replacement for radar-based ADAS, it serves as an effective educational prototype and entry-level safety aid. Future work includes multi-sensor fusion and wireless dashboard integration.

title: AN E-COMMERCE CONTROL UNIT FOR ADDRESSING ONLINE TRANSACTIONS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES: SAUDI ARABIA—CASE STUDY
author: Omar Saeed Al-Mushayt, Wajeb Gharibi, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: E-commerce in developing countries like Saudi Arabia faces challenges including payment fraud, lack of consumer trust, and fragmented regulatory frameworks. This paper proposes a smart e-commerce control unit—a policy and technology framework—to enhance transaction security, reliability, and competitiveness.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The study analyzes Saudi Arabia’s e-commerce landscape through stakeholder interviews, policy review, and case studies of local platforms (e.g., Noon, Amazon.sa). The proposed control unit integrates: (1) secure payment gateways, (2) AI-driven fraud detection, (3) standardized return policies, and (4) government-backed digital trust seals.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Pilot implementation with 3 SMEs shows a 40% reduction in chargebacks and 35% increase in customer trust (measured via post-purchase surveys). The control unit aligns with Saudi Vision 2030’s digital economy goals. Key success factors include regulatory support and interoperability with existing banking infrastructure.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: A holistic control unit combining technology, policy, and consumer education can overcome e-commerce barriers in emerging markets. The Saudi case offers a replicable model for other developing nations. Future work will explore blockchain for transparent transaction logging and cross-border payment harmonization.

title: CROSS-LAYER DESIGN ON SOFTWARE DEFINED VEHICULAR NETWORK (SDVN) BASED ON RADIO ACCESS TECHNOLOGY (RAT) IEEE 802.11BD TO IMPROVE END-TO-END COMMUNICATION PERFORMANCE
author: Galih Nugraha Nurkahfi, Nana Rachmana Syambas, Eueung Mulyana, Nasrullah Armi, Iyad Dayoub, Elhadj Dogheche, Syaiful Ahdan, Ratna Mayasari, Ridha Muldina Negara, Ade Nurhayati

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The rise of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and autonomous vehicles has intensified the demand for reliable vehicular communication. IEEE 802.11bd (the evolution of 802.11p) is a key Radio Access Technology (RAT) for Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication. However, in high-density traffic scenarios, signal blocking and interference severely degrade end-to-end performance. This paper addresses these challenges through a cross-layer design in a Software-Defined Vehicular Network (SDVN) architecture.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The proposed solution integrates cross-layer optimization between the physical and MAC layers within an SDVN framework. Specifically, it combines **Transmit Antenna Selection (TAS)** and **Transmit Power Adaptation (TPA)**, coordinated by a centralized SDN controller. The controller dynamically adjusts antenna configuration and power levels based on real-time channel state information (CSI), vehicle density, and link quality metrics. Simulations are conducted in OMNeT++/Veins with SUMO traffic models under urban scenarios with 50–200 vehicles/km².

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The cross-layer SDVN approach reduces packet loss by 42% and improves throughput by 37% compared to standard 802.11bd in dense traffic (150 vehicles/km²). End-to-end delay decreases from 85 ms to 52 ms, meeting URLLC requirements for safety-critical applications. TAS effectively mitigates non-line-of-sight (NLOS) blocking, while TPA minimizes co-channel interference without excessive energy consumption.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: By leveraging SDN’s global network view and cross-layer adaptability, the proposed design significantly enhances 802.11bd performance in challenging vehicular environments. This paves the way for scalable, reliable V2X communication in smart cities. Future work includes integration with 5G NR-V2X and machine learning-based predictive resource allocation.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A LOW-COST WEARABLE DEVICE FOR COVID-19 SELF-QUARANTINE MONITORING SYSTEM
author: Galih Nugraha Nurkahfi, Nasrullah Armi, Vita Awalia Mardiana, Mochamad Mardi Martadinata, Arumjeni Mitayani, Asih Setiarini, Budi Prawara, Dayat Kurniawan, Rizal Firmansyah, Ahmad Fauzi Rozie, Agus Arisal, Siti Setiana

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Effective quarantine enforcement during the pandemic requires affordable, scalable monitoring solutions. This study presents a low-cost wearable system that integrates geofencing, contact tracing, and real-time alerting using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and smartphone-based GPS, targeting resource-constrained public health programs.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system comprises a wearable BLE tag and a paired smartphone app. The wearable transmits unique IDs, while the phone handles GPS positioning, data logging, and communication with a central server. The server includes a dashboard, digital map, notification engine, and database. The design prioritizes low power consumption, with BLE advertising intervals optimized for battery longevity. Testing was conducted in lab and field environments.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The prototype achieves 94% location accuracy within 5-meter geofence boundaries and 89% proximity detection reliability at 1.5m distance. Battery life exceeds 72 hours with 10-second BLE intervals. System latency for violation alerts is under 8 seconds. The total hardware cost is below $15 per unit, making it viable for mass deployment in developing regions.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: This integrated, low-cost solution demonstrates that effective quarantine monitoring is achievable without expensive infrastructure. Future work includes integration with national health systems and adding biometric sensors (e.g., temperature) for symptom-based alerts.

title: COMMON MODE NOISE REDUCTION STRATEGIES IN RADAR DEVICES
author: Tjahjo Adiprabowo, Yuyu Wahyu, Budi Prawara, Nasrullah Armi, Budiman Putra Asma’Ur Rohman, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Common Mode Noise (CMN) significantly degrades radar signal integrity, reducing sensitivity and detection range. This paper evaluates multiple CMN mitigation strategies in practical radar hardware, focusing on cost-effective and implementable design techniques.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Eight strategies are analyzed: (1) differential transformers, (2) common-mode filters, (3) proper PCB layout, (4) low-noise component selection, (5) cable shielding, (6) ground plane separation, (7) digital signal processing, and (8) galvanic isolation. Each is implemented on a 24 GHz FMCW radar prototype, and noise reduction is quantified via spectrum analyzer and SNR measurements.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Proper PCB design emerges as the most impactful single technique, reducing CMN by 20%. When combined with common-mode filters and ground separation, total noise suppression reaches 45%. Differential signaling and galvanic isolation show marginal gains in this frequency band. The study provides a prioritized checklist for radar designers.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: CMN reduction is best achieved through holistic design rather than isolated fixes. PCB layout and grounding are foundational; filtering and component selection provide fine-tuning. These insights enable more robust, sensitive radar systems for automotive and industrial applications.

title: OPTIMIZATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF RASPBERRY PI 4 MODEL B FOR THE INTERNET OF THINGS
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Agoestina Mappadang, Nasrullah Armi, Arief Budi Santiko, Tjahjo Adiprabowo, Riza Zulkarnain, Adi Wirawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The Raspberry Pi 4 Model B offers significant performance improvements over predecessors, making it ideal for edge IoT applications. This paper explores its optimization for real-time data acquisition, processing, and cloud integration in resource-constrained environments.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The study configures Raspberry Pi 4 as an IoT edge node, interfacing with RF modules (LoRa, ZigBee) and sensors (temperature, motion). Python 3 scripts handle data collection, preprocessing, and transmission to cloud platforms (ThingSpeak, The Things Network). Power management, thermal throttling, and network latency are monitored under sustained load.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The Pi 4 achieves stable operation at 1.8 GHz with passive cooling, supporting 5 concurrent sensor streams with <100 ms latency. LoRa integration enables 2 km range in urban settings. CPU temperature remains below 70°C with lightweight OS (Raspberry Pi OS Lite). Power consumption averages 3.2W during active transmission.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Raspberry Pi 4 is a versatile, cost-effective platform for mid-complexity IoT deployments. Its balance of performance, connectivity, and power efficiency makes it suitable for smart agriculture, building automation, and educational projects. Future work includes containerized deployment and AI inference at the edge.

title: SIMULASI DAN ANALISIS JARINGAN ETHERNET PASSIVE OPTICAL NETWORK (EPON) UNTUK TELKOM CIPONDOH TANGERANG
author: Muhammad Irfan Alghiffari, Achmad Ali Muayyadi, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Passive Optical Network (PON) technology supports high-bandwidth triple-play services (data, voice, video) over a single fiber, making it ideal for dense urban areas like Cipondoh, Tangerang. This study simulates an EPON deployment to evaluate QoS performance against ITU-T standards.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Network simulation is performed using OPNET Modeler, modeling a tree topology with 1 OLT and 32 ONUs serving residential and business users. Traffic profiles include VoIP, IPTV, and internet data. Key QoS metrics—delay, jitter, throughput—are measured under peak load (80% utilization) and compared to ITU-T G.983 thresholds.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: All services meet ITU-T requirements: VoIP delay = 42 ms (<150 ms), IPTV jitter = 8 ms (<30 ms), and internet throughput = 92 Mbps (92% of 100 Mbps link). The system supports 1:32 split ratio without congestion. Fiber reach up to 20 km maintains BER < 10⁻⁹.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: EPON is a robust, scalable solution for Telkom’s fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) rollout in Cipondoh. The simulation validates its ability to deliver high-quality triple-play services. Future work includes dynamic bandwidth allocation (DBA) optimization for asymmetric traffic.

title: TIME SYNCHRONIZATION FOR OFDM SYSTEMS USING THE SYMMETRIC CORRELATOR-ELM TECHNIQUE
author: Suyoto Suyoto, Galih Nugraha Nurkahfi, Mohammad Hamdani, Vita Awalia Mardiana, Chaeriah Bin Ali Wael, Salita Ulitia Prini, Nasrullah Armi, Tati Mardiana, Nanang Ruhyana, Andri Agung Riyadi, Achmad Bayhaqy

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Accurate time synchronization is critical for OFDM systems to avoid inter-symbol interference (ISI). Multipath channels complicate synchronization, especially in mobile environments. This paper proposes a novel technique combining symmetric correlator metrics with an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) to enhance robustness.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The method uses a symmetric correlator to generate a coarse timing metric, which is then refined by an ELM network trained to suppress multipath-induced errors. Unlike conventional methods, it requires no prior channel statistics or length information. Performance is evaluated via synchronization error probability under Rayleigh fading channels.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The proposed technique reduces timing error probability by 58% compared to Schmidl & Cox and 32% versus autocorrelation-based methods at 10 dB SNR. ELM training converges in under 1 second, making it suitable for real-time implementation. The method maintains accuracy even with 10-tap multipath channels.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The symmetric correlator-ELM approach offers a low-complexity, high-accuracy solution for OFDM synchronization in challenging channels. Its data-driven nature makes it adaptable to diverse propagation environments without manual tuning.

title: RAPID AND EFFICIENT FACIAL LANDMARK IDENTIFICATION BY LIGHT AND HIGH RESOLUTION NETWORK USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
author: Saad Mamoun Abdel Rahman, Nasrullah Armi, Mohammed Eltahir Abdelhag, Sherif Tawfik Amin, Hassan Abu Eishah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Real-time facial landmark detection is essential for driver monitoring systems, but existing high-resolution networks suffer from high computational cost. This paper introduces THRN Plus—a lightweight, efficient architecture that maintains accuracy while reducing inference time.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: THRN Plus enhances the Tiny High-Resolution Network (THRN) with a novel fusion block and optimized output module. It processes multi-resolution feature maps in parallel and fuses them with reduced computational overhead. The model is trained on 300W and AFLW datasets and evaluated on CPU and embedded GPU.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: THRN Plus achieves 98.2% landmark detection accuracy (NME = 4.1%) on 300W, matching state-of-the-art models, but with 3.1× faster inference (18 ms/frame on Jetson Nano). The fusion block reduces FLOPs by 42% compared to baseline THRN, enabling real-time driver drowsiness detection.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: THRN Plus bridges the gap between accuracy and efficiency in facial landmark detection. Its design is ideal for edge-based driver monitoring and other latency-sensitive vision applications. Future work includes 3D landmark extension and occlusion handling.

title: FEDERATED META-LEARNING FOR TASK OFFLOADING AND RESOURCE ALLOCATION IN MEC-IOT
author: Bakhit Amine Adoum, Faitchou Marius Fidel, Samafou Faustin, Amir Moungache, Nasrullah Armi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) alleviates IoT device constraints by offloading tasks to nearby servers. However, dynamic workloads and heterogeneous requirements make optimal offloading challenging. This paper proposes a federated meta-learning framework that adapts to new tasks and devices without central data collection.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system uses federated learning to train a global meta-model across edge servers, while each device performs local adaptation via meta-learning (MAML-style).
