sections.content: Model 915 menunjukkan stabilitas terbaik dengan PSNR 28.4 dB. Transmisi gambar 128×128 membutuhkan bandwidth 89% lebih rendah daripada 512×512. Akurasi deteksi objek pada gambar hasil rekonstruksi: 92.3% (vs 94.1% pada asli). Latensi total: 210 ms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: SRCNN memungkinkan transmisi gambar efisien untuk kendaraan otonom di jaringan terbatas. Model 915 direkomendasikan untuk keseimbangan antara kecepatan dan kualitas. Penelitian selanjutnya akan menguji pada jaringan LoRa nyata.

title: Adjustment of PointPillars for Effective LiDAR-Based Object Detection and Classification in Constrained Environments
author: A. I. Nafian, D. Anggraini, M. I. Ardimansyah, Arief Suryadi Satyawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Kendaraan otonom BRIN beroperasi di lingkungan terbatas dengan objek spesifik (gerobak, tiang, tanaman) yang tidak tercakup dataset umum. PointPillars, meski efisien, kurang optimal untuk point cloud sparse dari LiDAR VLP-16.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Peneliti memodifikasi backbone PointPillars dengan ResNet (BaseBEVRESBackbone) dan mengurangi ukuran voxel menjadi 0.16m. Dataset lokal dikumpulkan di area kampus BRIN dengan anotasi 5 kelas objek. Pelatihan menggunakan loss focal dan optimizer AdamW.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Model modifikasi mencapai mAP 0.76, mengungguli PointPillars asli (0.68). Kecepatan inferensi: 22 FPS pada NVIDIA Jetson AGX. Deteksi gerobak dan tiang meningkat signifikan berkat penanganan point cloud sparse yang lebih baik.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Adaptasi PointPillars dengan backbone ResNet dan voxel kecil sangat efektif untuk lingkungan terbatas. Sistem ini telah diintegrasikan ke prototipe kendaraan otonom BRIN. Penelitian lanjutan akan menambahkan pelacakan multi-objek (tracking).

title: Enhancing Image Quality in Facial Recognition Systems with GAN-Based Reconstruction Techniques
author: Beni Wijaya, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Mokh Mirza Etnisa Haqiqi, Helfy Susilawati, Khaulyca Arva Artemysia, Sani Moch Sopian, M Ikbal Shamie

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Kualitas gambar wajah yang buruk akibat noise, oklusi, atau kompresi menyebabkan kegagalan sistem pengenalan wajah. Penelitian ini mengusulkan GAN berbasis residual blocks dan loss multi-skala untuk rekonstruksi wajah berkualitas tinggi.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Model GAN dimodifikasi dengan 6 varian arsitektur, menggabungkan loss adversarial, perceptual (VGG), dan rekonstruksi (L1). Dilatih pada dataset CelebA-HQ dan LFW yang dikorupsi. Evaluasi menggunakan PSNR, SSIM, dan validasi identitas dengan SFace.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Model terbaik mencapai PSNR 26.93, SSIM 0.90, dan confidence SFace >0.55. Rekonstruksi mempertahankan identitas meskipun dengan oklusi 40%. Waktu inferensi: 85 ms per gambar pada RTX 3060.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Teknik GAN berbasis multi-loss secara signifikan meningkatkan kualitas dan keandalan pengenalan wajah. Sistem ini cocok untuk aplikasi keamanan, layanan publik, dan telemedicine di lingkungan dengan kualitas gambar terbatas.

title: Efficient Image Transmission for Autonomous Systems Using Residual Dense Feature Networks Over LoRa Networks
author: Muhamad Fadly Rizqy Praptawilaga, Galura Muhammad Suranegara, Arief Suryadi Satyawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Jaringan LoRa memiliki bandwidth sangat terbatas (0.3–50 kbps), membuat transmisi gambar tampak mustahil. Penelitian ini memperkenalkan RDF Net—jaringan super-resolusi yang mengirim gambar 40×40 dan merekonstruksi menjadi 800×800 di sisi penerima.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: RDF Net menggabungkan Contrast-Aware Channel Attention (CCA), Enhanced Spatial Attention (ESA), dan Blueprint Separable Convolution (BSConv). Dilatih pada dataset gambar jalan dan objek perkotaan. Simulasi transmisi menggunakan model LoRa dengan data rate 50 kbps.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Model-4 (CCA+ESA) mencapai SSIM 0.88 dan PSNR 25.1 dB. Waktu transmisi gambar 40×40: 0.21–0.56 detik. Meski tidak real-time penuh, sistem ini layak untuk aplikasi non-kritis seperti pemantauan jarak jauh atau diagnosa kendaraan.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: RDF Net membuka kemungkinan transmisi visual di jaringan ultra-low-bandwidth. Ini sangat berguna untuk kendaraan otonom di daerah terpencil. Penelitian selanjutnya akan menguji pada perangkat LoRa nyata dan mengeksplorasi kompresi adaptif.

title: IMPLEMENTASI MASK R-CNN UNTUK APLIKASI SEGMENTASI OBJEK SUATU AREA DARI UDARA
author: Raihan Aura Ferdiansyah, Suharjanto Utomo, Arief Suryadi Satyawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Segmentasi instance dari citra udara memungkinkan identifikasi dan pelacakan objek individual seperti bangunan, sawah, dan landasan. Mask R-CNN, sebagai perluasan Faster R-CNN, menawarkan segmentasi pixel-level yang akurat.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Dataset 1.200 citra udara dari Google Earth Pro diannotasi menggunakan VIA. Model dilatih dengan IMAGE_MIN/MAX_DIM=512, LEARNING_RATE=0.001, dan batch size 2. Augmentasi mencakup rotasi dan perubahan kecerahan.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Model mencapai mAP 0.8182 dan akurasi segmentasi 63%. Sawah dan landasan tersegmentasi dengan baik (akurasi >80%), tetapi bangunan hanya 51.02% karena variasi bentuk dan bayangan kompleks.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Mask R-CNN efektif untuk segmentasi objek dari udara, terutama untuk objek dengan bentuk teratur. Untuk bangunan, diperlukan dataset lebih besar dan augmentasi geometris. Sistem ini mendukung aplikasi drone untuk pemantauan pertanian dan perencanaan kota.

title: Thermal Image-Based Multi-Class Semantic Segmentation for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation in Restricted Environments
author: Nurul Fazri, Helfy Susilawati, Mokh Mirza Etnisa Haqiqi, Arief Suryadi Satyawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Navigasi kendaraan otonom di malam hari atau kabut memerlukan segmentasi semantik berbasis citra termal. SegNet, dengan arsitektur encoder-decoder simetris, dipilih untuk tugas ini karena efisiensinya dalam segmentasi piksel-level.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: 3.001 citra termal diambil di lingkungan urban dan diannotasi untuk 10 kelas (motor, tiang, pohon, bangunan, dll.). Model SegNet dilatih selama 120 epoch dengan optimizer SGD dan learning rate 0.01.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Akurasi pelatihan: 96.7%, loss akhir: 0.096. F1-score tertinggi: tiang (0.84), motor (0.63). F1-score terendah: bangunan (0.34), pohon (0.42) karena kompleksitas tekstur dan bentuk. Segmentasi objek terdefinisi jelas sangat akurat.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: SegNet menunjukkan potensi besar untuk segmentasi citra termal dalam navigasi otonom. Untuk objek kompleks, diperlukan model berbasis attention atau transformer. Penelitian ini mendukung pengembangan sistem navigasi all-weather untuk kendaraan otonom.

title: Optimized CNN-Based Autoencoder for Efficient Image Compression in LoRa Networks for Autonomous Electric Vehicles
author: Reza Nurfaudzan Ash Shiddiq, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Galura Muhammad Suranegara, Muhammad Iqbal Fauzan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Kompresi gambar efisien diperlukan untuk transmisi data visual kendaraan otonom melalui jaringan LoRa yang berbandwidth rendah. Autoencoder berbasis CNN menawarkan kompresi lossy yang dapat dipelajari.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Autoencoder CNN dioptimalkan dengan lapisan bottleneck 128-dimensi. Teknik tambahan: Adaptive Quantization, Huffman Encoding, dan Zlib Compression. Dilatih pada gambar 80×80 dari simulator kendaraan otonom. Loss function: kombinasi MSE dan SSIM.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Sistem mencapai PSNR rata-rata >24 dB dengan rasio kompresi 15:1. Ukuran file akhir: ~1.2 KB per gambar. Transmisi melalui simulasi LoRa (50 kbps) membutuhkan ~0.2 detik per gambar. Rekonstruksi mempertahankan fitur penting untuk deteksi objek.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Autoencoder CNN yang dioptimalkan memungkinkan kompresi gambar yang sangat efisien untuk jaringan LoRa. Ini membuka jalan bagi aplikasi telemetri visual pada kendaraan otonom di daerah terpencil. Penelitian selanjutnya akan mengintegrasikan dengan sistem deteksi objek end-to-end.

title: Restorasi Citra Wajah Terdegradasi Menggunakan Model GAN dan Fungsi Loss
author: Beni Wijaya, Mokh Mirza Etnisa Haqiqi, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Helfy Susilawati

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Citra wajah yang terdegradasi akibat oklusi atau kerusakan mengganggu sistem pengenalan wajah dan aplikasi forensik. Penelitian ini mengembangkan model GAN berbasis encoder-decoder dengan skip connection dan residual block untuk merekonstruksi area wajah yang hilang secara realistis.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Dataset terdiri dari 1.000 pasang citra (500 asli + 500 dengan oklusi buatan). Model dilatih selama 50 epoch menggunakan loss adversarial dan rekonstruksi. Arsitektur mencakup 4 residual blocks dan skip connections untuk mempertahankan detail tingkat tinggi. Evaluasi dilakukan secara kualitatif dan melalui stabilitas loss.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Loss generator menurun dari 0.80 ke 0.67, sementara loss discriminator stabil di 0.70. Rekonstruksi fitur wajah (mata, hidung, mulut) menunjukkan ketelitian visual tinggi. Artefak minor muncul pada area tekstur kompleks seperti rambut, tetapi struktur wajah tetap konsisten.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Model GAN yang diusulkan efektif dalam restorasi wajah terdegradasi. Pendekatan ini mendukung aplikasi keamanan dan digital forensics. Rekomendasi: perluasan dataset dengan variasi etnis dan kondisi pencahayaan, serta eksplorasi arsitektur berbasis attention.

title: Optimizing Autonomous Navigation: Advances in LiDAR-based Object Recognition with Modified Voxel-RCNN
author: Firman, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Helfy Susilawati, Mokh Mirza Etnisa Haqiqi, Khaulyca Arva Artemysia, Sani Moch Sopian, Beni Wijaya, Muhammad Ikbal Samie

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Kendaraan otonom memerlukan deteksi objek 3D yang akurat di lingkungan dinamis. Penelitian ini meningkatkan Voxel-RCNN untuk pengenalan objek berbasis LiDAR dalam skenario terbatas, dengan fokus pada enam kelas: manusia, mobil, sepeda, pohon, gerobak, dan dinding.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Dataset point cloud dikonversi ke format KITTI. Dua modifikasi utama diterapkan pada Voxel-RCNN: (1) peningkatan backbone dengan residual connections, (2) optimasi voxel size dan anchor design. Model dilatih selama 600 epoch dan dievaluasi menggunakan mAP, precision, recall, dan F1-score.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Modification 2 meningkatkan skor deteksi 3D untuk mobil (skenario sulit) dari 4.39 ke 10.31. Modification 3 mencapai loss pelatihan terendah (1.68) dan mengurangi loss hingga 29.1%. Namun, kinerja dunia nyata menunjukkan perlunya keseimbangan antara akurasi pelatihan dan generalisasi.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Modifikasi Voxel-RCNN secara signifikan meningkatkan deteksi objek LiDAR untuk navigasi otonom. Sistem ini telah diintegrasikan ke prototipe kendaraan BRIN. Penelitian lanjutan akan mengeksplorasi pelacakan multi-objek dan sensor fusion dengan kamera.

title: Enhancing Negative Film Colorization through Systematic CycleGAN Architectural Modifications: A Comprehensive Analysis of Generator and Discriminator Performance
author: Khaulyca Arva Artemysia, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Mokhammad Mirza Etnisa Haqiqi, Helfy Susilawati, Beni Wijaya, Sani Moch Sopian, Muhammad Ikbal Shamie, Firman

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Film negatif memiliki tantangan unik: inversi warna dan kehilangan detail. Penelitian ini memodifikasi CycleGAN untuk colorisasi film negatif digital, fokus pada arsitektur jaringan tanpa metrik eksternal seperti PSNR atau FID.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Dataset: 500 citra negatif + 500 citra warna tidak berpasangan. 19 modifikasi arsitektur diuji secara individual, termasuk penambahan residual blocks, perubahan jumlah filter, fungsi aktivasi, dan koneksi antar lapisan. Evaluasi berdasarkan stabilitas loss generator/discriminator dan kualitas visual.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Modification 4 paling optimal: loss generator (G: 2.39–4.07, F: 2.82–3.66), discriminator (D_X: 0.36–0.93, D_Y: 0.15–1.39). Hasil colorisasi lebih akurat dan estetis dibanding baseline, dengan konsistensi warna dan detail yang lebih baik.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Modifikasi arsitektur CycleGAN secara sistematis dapat meningkatkan kualitas colorisasi film negatif. Pendekatan ini membuka jalan untuk pelestarian arsip film analog secara digital. Penelitian selanjutnya akan mengintegrasikan metrik persepsi dan dataset lebih besar.

title: Development of a Modified CycleGAN Model with Residual Blocks and Perceptual Loss for Image Dehazing
author: Sani Moch Sopian, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Mokhammad Mirza Etnisa Haqiqi, Helfy Susilawati, Beni Wijaya, Khaulyca Arva Artemysia, Muhammad Ikbal Samie

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Kabut mengurangi kontras dan kejelasan citra, mengganggu aplikasi seperti kendaraan otonom dan penginderaan jauh. Penelitian ini mengusulkan modifikasi CycleGAN untuk dehazing citra tunggal menggunakan data tidak berpasangan.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sepuluh varian arsitektur dikembangkan dengan kombinasi: residual blocks, attention mechanism, perceptual loss (VGG19), dan haze-aware loss. Dataset terdiri dari citra berkabut dan jernih. Evaluasi menggunakan PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, dan analisis visual.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Modification 10 (perceptual + haze-aware loss) terbaik: PSNR 7.99, SSIM 0.4202, LPIPS 0.6577. Loss generator stabil (G: 0.91, F: 0.57), menunjukkan keseimbangan antara realisme dan akurasi. Citra hasil lebih tajam dengan detail tepi yang terpelihara.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: CycleGAN yang dimodifikasi secara signifikan meningkatkan kualitas dehazing. Integrasi perceptual loss membuktikan pentingnya mempertimbangkan persepsi manusia dalam restorasi citra. Model ini siap diuji pada sistem kendaraan otonom nyata.

title: Enhancing Hazy Image Dehazing Using a Modified CycleGAN
author: Sani Moch Sopian, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Mokhammad Mirza Etnisa Haqiqi, Helfy Susilawati, Rifki Nurpalah, Nizar Alam Hamdani

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Dehazing citra berkabut sangat penting untuk sistem visi mesin. Penelitian ini menyempurnakan CycleGAN dengan modifikasi arsitektur untuk meningkatkan kinerja dehazing pada data tidak berpasangan dalam skenario dunia nyata.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Dataset: 50 citra berkabut + 50 citra jernih. Sepuluh modifikasi generator diuji, menggabungkan residual blocks, dilated convolutions, self-attention, dan loss tambahan. Pelatihan dilakukan secara unsupervised. Evaluasi menggunakan PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, dan analisis visual.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Modification 5 menunjukkan keseimbangan terbaik antara stabilitas pelatihan dan kualitas output. Meski PSNR tidak tertinggi, citra hasil memiliki kontras lebih baik dan detail lebih alami dibanding baseline. Self-attention terbukti efektif dalam mempertahankan konteks global.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Modifikasi arsitektur CycleGAN meningkatkan kemampuan dehazing tanpa data berpasangan. Pendekatan ini mendukung aplikasi kendaraan otonom di daerah berkabut seperti dataran tinggi. Penelitian selanjutnya akan menguji pada dataset lebih besar dan kondisi cuaca beragam.

title: Cooperative game theory approach for energy-efficient node clustering in wireless sensor network
author: Salita Ulitia Prini, Winy Desvasari, Rico Dahlan, Ros Sariningrum

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) consist of battery-powered nodes with limited energy, making energy efficiency a critical design goal. Clustering is a proven technique to extend network lifetime, and game theory offers a mathematical framework for optimizing cooperative behavior among nodes.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The paper proposes a Cooperative Game Theoretic Clustering (CGC) algorithm based on a 3-agent cost-sharing game. Cluster heads form coalitions to share energy costs for data aggregation and transmission. Performance is compared against LEACH in terms of First Node Dies (FND), Half Node Dies (HND), and total residual energy via MATLAB simulations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: CGC improves network stability: FND increases by 65% and HND by 52.4% compared to LEACH. Total residual energy is higher due to balanced load distribution. However, as node count exceeds 150, LEACH’s simplicity gives it a slight edge in scalability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: CGC demonstrates that cooperative game theory can significantly enhance energy efficiency in small-to-medium WSNs. For large-scale deployments, hybrid approaches combining game theory with lightweight protocols may be optimal. The study validates the role of strategic cooperation in sustainable sensor networking.

title: WiFi-AC Based Telecommunication Infrastructure for Autonomous Vehicle in Limited Area
author: Galih Nugraha Nurkahfi, Vita Awalia Mardiana, Arumjeni Mitayani, Mochamad Mardi Marta Dinata, Dikdik Krisnandi, Arief Suryadi Satyawan, Ana Heryana, Andri Fachrur Rozie

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: IEEE 802.11p is the standard for vehicular communication but suffers from high cost and limited availability. This research explores IEEE 802.11ac (WiFi-AC) as a cost-effective alternative for autonomous vehicle communication in confined areas like office complexes or campuses.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A testbed was built using commercial WiFi-AC access points in a residential road within an office area. Key QoS metrics—throughput, delay, jitter, and packet loss—were measured under varying traffic loads using iPerf and Wireshark.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system achieved average throughput of 185 Mbps, delay of 8.2 ms, jitter of 0.4 ms, and packet loss <0.1%. Performance remained stable with up to 10 concurrent vehicles. The solution is 70% cheaper than 802.11p-based infrastructure.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: WiFi-AC is a viable, high-performance, and economical communication backbone for autonomous vehicles in limited areas. It is ideal for pilot deployments and educational prototypes. Future work includes integration with 5G for seamless handover in hybrid networks.

title: Robust time synchronization for NC-OFDM cognitive radio systems
author: Suyoto Suyoto, Sugihartono Sugihartono, Iskandar Iskandar, Adit Kurniawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Non-Contiguous OFDM (NC-OFDM) is widely used in cognitive radio to utilize fragmented spectrum. However, time synchronization in NC-OFDM is challenged by multipath channels, narrowband interference (NBI), and sparse subcarrier allocation.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The proposed method uses a correlation-based metric that does not require prior knowledge of subcarrier positions or NBI center frequency. It leverages guard interval properties and is robust to high delay-spread channels. Performance is evaluated under AWGN and multipath fading (ITU-R Vehicular A).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The method achieves timing error probability of <10⁻⁴ at SNR = 5 dB, outperforming conventional Schmidl & Cox by 32%. It remains effective under 20% NBI occupancy and delay spreads up to 1.2 μs. Complexity is low, suitable for real-time implementation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: This synchronization technique enhances NC-OFDM reliability in dynamic spectrum access scenarios. Its robustness to interference and channel dispersion makes it suitable for next-generation cognitive radio systems. The design is compatible with existing CR hardware with minimal modification.

title: Pelatihan Analisa Data Youtube dan Website untuk Majelis Remaja dan Pemuda Islam (MADARIS) Jakarta Islamic Centre
author: Achmad Bayhaqy, Andri Agung Riyadi, Suyoto Suyoto, Nanang Ruhyana

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Organizations like MADARIS need to understand audience behavior to create engaging digital content. However, many lack skills in data analytics. This community service introduces Google Analytics and YouTube Analytics to empower youth leaders in data-driven content strategy.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A hands-on workshop was conducted for MADARIS members, covering: (1) setting up Google Analytics, (2) interpreting traffic sources and user behavior, (3) analyzing YouTube watch time and audience retention, and (4) using insights to improve content relevance.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Participants successfully implemented analytics on their website and YouTube channel. Post-training, content engagement increased by 45% (measured by average session duration and watch time). 92% of participants reported improved confidence in digital outreach.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Basic data literacy significantly enhances the digital impact of community organizations. The training model is replicable for other religious or social groups. Future sessions will include social media analytics and A/B testing for content optimization.

title: Autonomous radar interference detection and mitigation using neural network and signal decomposition
author: Dayat Kurniawan, Budiman Putra Asmaur Rohman, Ratna Indrawijaya, Chaeriah Bin Ali Wael, Suyoto Suyoto, Purwoko Adhi, Iman Firmansyah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Radar interference from nearby autonomous vehicles degrades detection performance by lowering SINR. Traditional mitigation methods struggle with dynamic, overlapping signals. This paper proposes a hybrid approach combining neural networks and variational mode decomposition (VMD).

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A 4-input neural network (SNR, mean, THD, RMS) detects interference. Mitigation uses VMD to decompose the signal into sub-bands, followed by CFAR-Z thresholding. The system is tested on FMCW radar signals with multiple interferers under varying SNR and bandwidth conditions.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The NN-VMD-CFAR-Z method increases SINR by up to 2 dB compared to NN-CFAR-Z. Detection accuracy exceeds 96% at SNR > 0 dB. VMD effectively isolates interference components, enabling precise zeroing without distorting the target signal.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The proposed method offers a robust, adaptive solution for radar interference in dense autonomous environments. It balances detection accuracy and computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time automotive radar systems. Future work includes hardware-in-the-loop validation.

title: Qu-Antri: Multi-tenant Architecture for Bandung Public Services to Reduce the Crowd
author: Wiwin Suwarningsih, Ana Heryana, Hilman F Pardede, Purwoko Adhi, Vicky Zilvan, Andri Fachrur Rozie, R Budiarianto Suryo Kusumo, Ekasari Nugraheni, R Sandra Yuwana, Dianadewi Riswantini, Endang Suryawati, Ade Ramdan, Dikdik Krisnandi, Andria Arisal

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Long queues in public services cause inefficiency and health risks, especially during pandemics. This research proposes Qu-Antri—a multi-tenant queuing system for Bandung city services that supports flexible deployment models: complete multi-tenant, single-tenant database, and single-tenant multi-service.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system was designed using UML (use case, activity, class, and sequence diagrams). Three architectures were implemented: (1) shared database/schema, (2) isolated databases on cloud servers with RESTful APIs, and (3) unified frontend with service-specific mockups. Testing was conducted via interactive user trials across 5 public service offices.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The prototype reduced average waiting time by 62% and physical crowding by 78%. The multi-tenant model showed 99.2% uptime and handled 500+ concurrent users. Users rated the interface 4.3/5 for ease of use. The system is now piloted in Bandung’s civil registration and health service offices.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Qu-Antri demonstrates that multi-tenant architecture can effectively digitize public services in urban Indonesia. Future work includes integration with national identity systems and AI-based appointment optimization.

title: Deep convolutional neural networks-based features for Indonesian large vocabulary speech recognition
author: Hilman F Pardede, Purwoko Adhi, Vicky Zilvan, Ade Ramdan, Dikdik Krisnandi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Indonesian speech recognition lags behind mainstream languages due to limited training data. This paper proposes a discriminatively trained CNN to extract robust acoustic features for large vocabulary continuous speech recognition (LVCSR) in Indonesian.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A CNN is trained end-to-end on Indonesian speech corpus (120 hours) using CTC loss. Features are fed to a hybrid HMM-DNN decoder. The model uses 4 convolutional layers with ReLU and batch normalization. Performance is evaluated using Word Error Rate (WER) on test sets of formal and conversational speech.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The CNN-based system achieves WER of 18.7% on formal speech and 24.3% on conversational speech, outperforming traditional GMM-HMM (32.1%) and generative DNN (26.8%). Training converges in 48 hours on a single GPU, demonstrating efficiency even with moderate data.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Discriminative CNN training is highly effective for low-resource languages like Indonesian. The approach bridges the gap between data-rich and data-poor languages. Future work includes multilingual transfer learning and integration with language models.

title: A generalization of sigmoid loss function using tsallis statistics for binary classification
author: Hilman F Pardede, Purwoko Adhi, Vicky Zilvan, Asri R Yuliani, Andria Arisal

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Standard sigmoid loss assumes Gaussian noise, which may not hold for imbalanced or noisy datasets. This paper generalizes the sigmoid loss using Tsallis q-exponential statistics, enabling adaptive slope control for robust binary classification.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The q-sigmoid loss is derived from Tsallis entropy, with parameter q controlling tail behavior. When q → 1, it reduces to standard sigmoid. The loss is integrated into logistic regression and neural networks. Evaluated on 8 UCI datasets with varying imbalance ratios (1:1 to 1:10).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Optimal q = 1.3–1.5 consistently improves F1-score by 4–9% over standard sigmoid, especially on imbalanced data. Training stability is maintained, and convergence speed is comparable. The method also reduces overfitting in small datasets.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Tsallis-based loss generalization offers a simple yet powerful way to enhance classifier robustness. It requires no architecture change and is plug-and-play compatible with existing frameworks. The approach is promising for medical and fraud detection applications.

title: Transformer with time vector representation for remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
author: Apik Wulan Sari, Asri Rizki Yuliani, Hilman Ferdinandus Pardede, Ade Ramdan, Winita Sulandari, Vicky Zilvan, Purwoko Adhi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Accurate prediction of lithium-ion battery Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is critical for electric vehicles and grid storage. Traditional models like LSTM struggle with long-term dependencies. This paper proposes a Transformer-based RUL predictor enhanced with Time2Vec for temporal encoding.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The model uses NASA’s battery dataset (B0005–B0018). Input features: voltage, current, temperature, and cycle count. Time2Vec encodes time steps into dense vectors. A 4-layer Transformer with self-attention predicts RUL. Compared against LSTM, GRU, and SVR.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The proposed method achieves RMSE of 48.2 cycles and MAE of 36.7, outperforming LSTM (RMSE: 67.4) by 28%. Attention maps reveal that voltage decay rate and temperature spikes are key predictors. Inference time: 12 ms per prediction on RTX 3060.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Transformer + Time2Vec provides superior RUL prediction by capturing long-range temporal patterns. The model is suitable for real-time battery management systems. Future work includes online learning and uncertainty quantification.

title: Blocking Object Effect in Propagation Channel of Millimeter Wave Wireless Communication
author: Hana Arisesa, Sevia M Idrus, Farabi Iqbal, Yusuf Nur Wijayanto, Purwoko Adhi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication is highly sensitive to blockage. This paper experimentally investigates the impact of common materials on 300 GHz wireless links using a photonic-based transmitter and electronic receiver.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A 10 Gbps link was tested over 8 cm using an optical frequency comb generator (OFCG). Five blocking objects (wood, plastic, glass, human hand, metal) were placed at various positions. BER was measured using a BERTScope with PRBS 27-1 pattern.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Minimum BER: 0.864×10⁻³ in clear LOS. Metal caused complete link failure. Human hand increased BER to 10⁻¹, glass to 10⁻², while plastic and wood had minimal impact (<2× BER increase). Even partial blockage degraded performance significantly due to narrow beamwidth.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: 300 GHz links are viable only in strict LOS with no human or metallic obstruction. The results inform antenna placement and redundancy design for indoor THz networks. Future work includes beam steering and MIMO for blockage mitigation.

title: Improved autocorrelation method for time synchronization in filtered orthogonal frequency division multiplexing
author: Arumjeni Mitayani, Purwoko Adhi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Filtered OFDM (F-OFDM) enables flexible subband allocation but degrades time synchronization when training symbols occupy only one subband. Standard autocorrelation (AC) methods suffer from low correlation peaks and timing ambiguity.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The paper proposes an averaging technique on the AC timing metric across multiple OFDM symbols. Simulations use F-OFDM with 1024 subcarriers, 1 subband for training, and AWGN/multipath channels. Performance is measured by timing error probability and mean squared error (MSE).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The improved AC method reduces timing MSE by 63% at SNR = 0 dB compared to standard AC. Peak-to-average ratio of the timing metric increases by 4.2×, enabling more reliable threshold-based detection. Complexity overhead is negligible (<5% CPU increase).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Simple averaging significantly enhances time synchronization in subband-limited F-OFDM. The method is compatible with 5G NR and beyond. Future work includes joint time-frequency synchronization and hardware implementation.

title: Fast prediction of a high directivity antenna characterization for future wireless communication based on terahertz photonics
author: Hana Arisesa, Yusuf Nur Wijayanto, Purwoko Adhi, Farabi Iqbal, Sevia M Idrus

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Characterizing high-directivity antennas at THz frequencies is time-consuming with traditional far-field methods. This research presents a fast near-field to far-field (NF-FF) transformation using terahertz photonics for J-band Cassegrain antennas.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A non-polarimetric electro-optic (EO) down-conversion system generates and detects THz signals. Near-field amplitude and phase are measured on a 2D plane. Far-field patterns are synthesized using NF-FF transformation. Results are validated against ITU-R F.699 recommendations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The synthesized E-plane and H-plane patterns match ITU standards within 1.2 dB. Measurement time reduced from 8 hours (far-field) to 45 minutes (near-field). The method accurately captures effects of sub-reflector and support rods on sidelobe levels.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: THz photonic-based NF-FF characterization enables rapid antenna validation for 6G and beyond. The approach is scalable to higher frequencies and complex antenna arrays. Future work includes real-time beam pattern monitoring.

title: UWB Radar Self-Motion Cancelation for Through-Wall Vital Sign Detection
author: Budiman PA Rohman, Masahiko Nishimoto, Ratna Indrawijaya, Dayat Kurniawan, Iman Firmansyah, Purwoko Adhi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Through-wall vital sign detection is critical for search and rescue, but radar motion (e.g., on drones) introduces severe clutter that masks weak respiratory signals. This paper proposes a self-motion cancellation technique using sequential image processing.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A UWB radar is mounted on a platform with controlled vertical drift. Range-Doppler maps are processed frame-by-frame. Motion artifacts are estimated from background regions and subtracted. Respiratory signals are extracted via bandpass filtering and peak detection.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The method successfully detects respiration at 0.3 Hz through a 10 cm concrete wall, even with ±5 cm radar motion. Signal-to-clutter ratio improves by 14 dB. Detection accuracy: 96.2% for live subjects vs. 2.1% false alarm for mannequins.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Self-motion cancellation enables reliable vital sign detection from non-stationary platforms like drones. The technique is low-complexity and real-time capable. Future work includes heartbeat detection and multi-target tracking.

title: Characterization of Tropical Leaf Properties Considering Millimeter Wave Wireless
author: Hana Arisesa, Sevia Mahdaliza Idrus Sutan Nameh, Farabi Iqbal, Yusuf Nur Wijayanto, Purwoko Adhi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Tropical vegetation affects mmWave propagation in urban and rural Indonesia. This study characterizes the dielectric properties of guava leaves (Psidium guajava) at Ka-band (26–40 GHz) for wireless planning and environmental sensing.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Fresh and dried guava leaves were measured using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) with waveguide transmission/reflection method. S-parameters were used to extract complex permittivity and permeability via Nicolson-Ross-Weir algorithm.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Fresh leaves show high permittivity (ε' ≈ 12–18) and loss tangent (tan δ ≈ 0.8–1.2) due to water content. Dried leaves have ε' ≈ 3–5 and tan δ ≈ 0.1–0.3. Attenuation through a single leaf: 8–14 dB at 30 GHz. Results align with Debye relaxation models.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Tropical foliage causes significant mmWave attenuation, necessitating dense base station deployment in green areas. The data supports foliage-aware channel models and dual-use applications in precision agriculture. Dataset is publicly released for research.

title: Experimental evaluation of cognitive frequency UAV-Radar for disaster search and rescue mission
author: Budiman PA Rohman, Ratna Indrawijaya, Dayat Kurniawan, Purwoko Adhi, Bagus Edy Sukoco

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Post-disaster search and rescue requires rapid, interference-resilient life detection. This paper presents a cognitive frequency UAV-radar that dynamically selects clean spectrum bands to enhance vital sign detection in rubble.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The UAV-radar scans 1–6 GHz in 100 MHz steps, selects the least noisy band via spectrum sensing, and transmits FMCW signals. Vital signs are extracted using micro-Doppler analysis. Tested on human subjects under concrete debris with competing RF sources (WiFi, LTE).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Cognitive frequency selection improves detection SNR by 9–12 dB compared to fixed-frequency radar. It successfully distinguishes unconscious survivors (respiration: 0.2–0.4 Hz) from deceased (no signal) with 98.7% accuracy. Mission time reduced by 34% due to fewer false alarms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Cognitive UAV-radar significantly enhances disaster response efficiency. The system is deployable within 5 minutes and operates for 45 minutes on battery. Future work includes AI-based victim classification and swarm coordination.

title: Three-dimensional printed asymmetric biconical antenna for borehole concrete sensing application
author: Dion H Fandiantoro, Naoki Matsunaga, Budiman Putra Asma’ur Rohman, Masahiko Nishimoto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Corrosion of reinforcing bars in concrete structures is a major safety concern. Borehole radar offers a non-destructive solution, but requires compact, high-performance antennas that fit narrow drill holes. This paper proposes a 3D-printed asymmetric biconical antenna tailored for borehole inspection.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The antenna was designed with a 20 mm diameter to fit standard boreholes. It was fabricated using a 3D printer with PLA plastic and coated with copper tape for conductivity. Simulations and measurements were conducted in free space and embedded in concrete blocks with rebars.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The antenna operates from 2.4 GHz (free space) down to 2.1 GHz (in concrete) up to 8 GHz. Reflection coefficient (S11) remains below -10 dB across the band. The asymmetric design improves impedance matching in lossy concrete environments compared to symmetric counterparts.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The 3D-printed antenna is a low-cost, customizable solution for borehole radar systems. Its compact size and robust performance make it ideal for civil infrastructure health monitoring. Future work includes integration with UWB radar for real-time corrosion mapping.

title: Optimized 2D CA-CFAR for Drone-Mounted Radar Signal Processing Using Integral Image Algorithm
author: Budiman P.A. Rohman, Muhammad Bagus Andra, Masahiko Nishimoto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Drone-mounted UWB radar for search and rescue is limited by onboard computational power. Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detection is essential but computationally heavy. This paper optimizes 2D Cell-Averaging CFAR using the integral image algorithm for real-time processing.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The integral image technique precomputes cumulative sums to enable O(1) window sum calculation. The optimized CA-CFAR was implemented on a Raspberry Pi 4 mounted on a multisensory drone. Performance was evaluated in terms of processing time and detection accuracy on buried object scenarios.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Processing time reduced by 68% compared to standard sliding-window CFAR. The system achieved real-time operation (12 FPS) on 512×512 radar images. Detection accuracy remained above 94% for targets at 0.5–1.2 m depth.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Integral image-based CFAR enables efficient radar processing on resource-constrained drones. This approach is critical for large-area post-disaster surveys. Future work includes adaptive window sizing based on target size estimation.

title: Remote Human Respiration Detection Using Ultra-Wideband Impulse Radar Mounted on a Linearly Flying Platform
author: Budiman Putra Asmaur Rohman, Masahiko Nishimoto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: In large disaster zones, fast aerial vital sign detection is essential. However, radar on moving platforms suffers from motion-induced signal distortion. This paper proposes a method to extract respiration signals from hyperbolic patterns in radar data.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A UWB radar was mounted on a linear rail to simulate drone flight. Sequential image processing reconstructs hyperbolic traces from B-scan data. Respiration frequency is extracted via FFT after background subtraction and noise filtering.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Human respiration (0.2–0.4 Hz) was detected at distances up to 3 m. Optimal platform speed: 0.5 m/s—faster speeds blurred hyperbolic patterns. SNR improved by 11 dB after processing. False alarm rate: <3% in controlled lab tests.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The method enables reliable respiration detection from linearly moving platforms. It provides design guidelines for drone speed in real missions. Future work includes 2D motion compensation and heartbeat detection.

title: Basic Shape Classification of Buried Object Using Pattern Matching in Ultrawideband Radar Image
author: Budiman PA Rohman, Masahiko Nishimoto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Identifying the shape of buried objects (e.g., pipes, rebars) improves interpretation of GPR data. This paper proposes a dynamic time warping (DTW)-based pattern matching technique for classifying cross-sectional shapes from UWB radar B-scans.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Reference patterns for circle, square, and triangle were generated via simulation and validated experimentally. DTW measures similarity between test and reference signals by aligning them non-linearly in time. Classification is based on minimum DTW distance.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The method achieved 92% accuracy in simulations and 87% in concrete experiments. DTW outperformed Euclidean distance by 23% in noisy conditions. Classification is robust to object depth and orientation variations within ±15°.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Pattern matching with DTW is a simple yet effective approach for shape-based object identification in radar imaging. It enhances automated interpretation of subsurface data. Future work includes 3D shape recognition and deep learning hybridization.

title: Reconstruction of Missing Ground-Penetrating Radar Traces Using Simplified U-Net
author: Budiman PA Rohman, Masahiko Nishimoto, Kohichi Ogata

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Missing traces in GPR data—caused by sensor failure or motion artifacts—degrade image quality and interpretation. This paper proposes a lightweight U-Net variant to reconstruct missing traces in reinforced concrete inspection.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The simplified U-Net uses shallow layers, reduced feature maps, multi-wide kernels, and fewer encoder-decoder steps. Trained on simulated and real GPR data of rebars and cracks. Input: incomplete B-scan; Output: reconstructed full B-scan.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The model achieves PSNR of 32.1 dB and SSIM of 0.93 on test data. Inference time: 18 ms per image on Jetson Nano. It outperforms linear interpolation and KNN by >8 dB in PSNR. Visual quality enables clear rebar detection even with 30% missing traces.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The lightweight U-Net is highly effective for GPR trace reconstruction on edge devices. It supports real-time data quality enhancement in field inspections. Code and dataset are publicly released for reproducibility.

title: Through-the-Wall Human Respiration Detection Using UWB Impulse Radar on Hovering Drone
author: Budiman Putra Asmaur Rohman, Muhammad Bagus Andra, Masahiko Nishimoto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Through-wall vital sign detection from drones is promising for search and rescue but challenged by drone vibration and weak respiration signals. This paper introduces a subspace-based signal processing method to enhance detection robustness.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Analytic signal representation is used to extract phase information. Subspace component segregation separates respiration from clutter and vibration. Tested on a hovering drone with artificial wall (10 cm concrete) and human subject behind it.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The method suppresses drone-induced vibration by 14 dB. Respiration detection accuracy: 96.3% at 1.5 m standoff distance. It works even with ±3 cm drone drift. False alarm rate for mannequins: 1.8%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Subspace-based processing enables reliable through-wall vital sign detection from unstable platforms. The system is deployable in real disaster scenarios. Future work includes multi-target tracking and heartbeat extraction.

title: Ultra-wideband Radar Signal Processing for Invisible Object Detection and Identification
author: Budiman Putra Asma’ur Rohman

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: UWB radar is effective for non-destructive testing and vital sign monitoring, but raw data is hard to interpret. This doctoral thesis proposes novel signal processing techniques to extract meaningful information from UWB responses.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Two main applications: (1) concrete inspection—estimating dielectric constant via analytic peak signal ratio to determine rebar depth/corrosion; (2) vital sign detection—motion compensation and micro-Doppler analysis. Methods include analytic signal processing, subspace filtering, and machine learning.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Dielectric constant estimation error <5% across concrete types. Rebar depth accuracy: ±2 mm. Respiration detection works at SNR as low as -10 dB. All methods are generalized across radar hardware, enabling wide applicability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The proposed techniques bridge the gap between raw UWB data and actionable insights. They are validated in both lab and field conditions. The thesis contributes foundational methods for next-generation radar-based sensing systems.

title: Phase Parameter Extraction from UWB Radar Response for Non-destructive Inspection
author: Masahiko Nishimoto, Budiman PA Rohman, Kohichi Ogata

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Corrosion changes the electromagnetic scattering phase of rebars, but traditional amplitude-based methods fail to capture this. This paper introduces a phase parameter for corrosion stage estimation in concrete.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: UWB radar responses from corroded rebars are analyzed in the frequency domain. A phase shift parameter is extracted from the scattering response. Simulations model rebars with 0–50% corrosion area. Performance is compared against correlation coefficient methods.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The phase parameter correlates strongly with corrosion level (R² = 0.94), while correlation coefficient fails (R² = 0.31) in high-noise scenarios. The method works even when rebar is deeply embedded (>10 cm).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Phase-based analysis provides a sensitive, noise-resilient indicator of rebar corrosion. It complements existing amplitude methods and enables quantitative structural health assessment. Future work includes field validation on real bridges.

title: Material Permittivity Estimation Using Analytic Peak Ratio of Air-Coupled GPR Signatures
author: Budiman PA Rohman, Masahiko Nishimoto, Kohichi Ogata

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Accurate permittivity estimation is crucial for depth calibration in GPR. Traditional methods require contact or reference objects. This paper proposes a contactless, air-coupled method using analytic peak ratio for mobile inspections.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The ratio of peak amplitudes between direct coupling and surface reflection is used to estimate permittivity. Reference curves are generated via FDTD simulation for common materials (concrete, asphalt, soil). Interpolation maps ratio to permittivity.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Permittivity estimation error: <4% for concrete (εᵣ = 4–8), <6% for soil (εᵣ = 3–15). Works across GPR types (1–3 GHz) and standoff distances (10–50 cm). Processing time: <100 ms per scan on embedded system.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The analytic peak ratio method enables fast, accurate permittivity estimation for large-area GPR surveys. It is ideal for drone or vehicle-mounted systems. The approach is now integrated into BRIN’s infrastructure inspection toolkit.

title: Moving Human Respiration Sign Detection Using mm-Wave Radar via Motion Path Reconstruction
author: Budiman PA Rohman, Manjunath Thindlu Rudrappa, Maksim Shargorodskyy, Reinhold Herschel, Masahiko Nishimoto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Detecting respiration from non-stationary humans (e.g., trapped victims moving slightly) is challenging. This paper proposes motion path reconstruction to separate vital signs from random body motion using mm-wave radar.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sequential radar frames undergo adaptive thresholding, image segmentation, and PCA-based motion path estimation. Respiration is extracted from the residual signal after motion compensation. Tested with human subjects moving randomly within ±20 cm.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system detects respiration with 93.7% accuracy despite random motion. Motion path reconstruction reduces clutter by 12 dB. Works at 24 GHz and 77 GHz bands. False alarm rate: 2.4% for static clutter.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Motion-aware processing enables robust vital sign detection in realistic post-disaster scenarios. The method is suitable for handheld or drone-based mm-wave radar systems. Future work includes integration with thermal cameras for multi-modal sensing.

title: Cognitive Linear Trajectory on GPR Imaging Using Lightweight Machine Learning
author: Ratna Indrawijaya, Budiman Putra Asma’ur Rohman

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) inspection of large structures like buildings or utility corridors is time-consuming. Fixed-speed scanning wastes time on empty regions. This paper proposes a cognitive linear trajectory that adapts scanning speed based on real-time object detection.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A lightweight 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) processes A-scan data to estimate the probability of subsurface objects. If an object is likely present, the GPR slows down to capture high-resolution data; otherwise, it speeds up. The system was evaluated on synthetic GPR data of rebars and voids.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The CNN achieved >80% accuracy in object existence detection. The adaptive trajectory reduced total scanning time by 35% while preserving image detail in regions of interest. Inference latency: <5 ms per A-scan on an embedded ARM Cortex-A72 processor.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Cognitive trajectory control enables efficient GPR surveying without sacrificing data quality. Future work includes real-world validation on concrete structures and integration with robotic scanning platforms.

title: Ground Penetrating Radar Data Inversion Using Dual-Input Convolutional Autoencoder for Ferroconcrete Inspection
author: Budiman Putra Asmaur Rohman, Masahiko Nishimoto, Ratna Indrawijaya, Dayat Kurniawan, Iman Firmansyah, Bagus Edy Sukoco

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: GPR B-scans are difficult to interpret for non-experts, especially in reinforced concrete inspection. This paper proposes a dual-input convolutional autoencoder to invert GPR scattering data into intuitive visualizations of internal structures (rebars, cracks).

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The model takes both amplitude and phase of GPR signals as dual inputs. A symmetric encoder-decoder architecture with skip connections reconstructs cross-sectional images. Training uses FDTD-simulated data for three scenarios: rebar-only, crack-only, and combined. Loss function combines MSE and structural similarity (SSIM).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The autoencoder achieves PSNR of 29.4 dB and SSIM of 0.88 on test data. Rebar diameter and crack width are visualized with <3 mm error. The model generalizes well across randomized concrete properties (permittivity 4–8, loss tangent 0.01–0.05).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Dual-input autoencoder significantly enhances GPR interpretability for civil engineers. The system is being integrated into BRIN’s infrastructure health monitoring toolkit. Future work includes real-data fine-tuning and 3D extension.

title: Comparing Predictive Capabilities of Machine Learning Models in Weather Forecasting
author: Chantika Rahma Galih Abu A’syifa, Brahmantya Aji Pramudita, Budiman Putra Asma’ur Rohman, Dhoni Putra Setiawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Weather forecasting is critical for agriculture, transport, and disaster preparedness. Traditional numerical models struggle with non-linear feature interactions and imbalanced data. This study evaluates four ML classifiers for short-term weather prediction.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Decision Tree, Random Forest, SVM, and XGBoost were trained on 5 years of meteorological data (temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed) from BMKG Indonesia. Task: classify next-day weather into 5 classes (sunny, cloudy, rain, heavy rain, storm). Metrics: accuracy, F1-score, and AUC-ROC.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: XGBoost outperformed others: accuracy = 92.3%, F1 = 0.91. Random Forest was close (89.7%), while SVM and Decision Tree lagged (<85%). XGBoost handled class imbalance best, especially for rare 'storm' events (recall = 84%).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: XGBoost is the most robust ML model for operational weather forecasting in tropical climates. The system is being piloted with local agricultural cooperatives. Future work includes ensemble methods and satellite data integration.

title: Optimizing Machine Learning for Imbalanced Rainfall Data Prediction
author: Rischa Zefaniya Br Sinulingga, Brahmantya Aji Pramudita, Budiman Putra Asma’ur Rohman, Dhoni Putra Setiawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Rainfall prediction is vital for flood and landslide mitigation, but datasets are highly imbalanced (few extreme rainfall events). Standard ML models bias toward majority classes. This paper evaluates resampling and cost-sensitive techniques to improve minority class prediction.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: SMOTE, ADASYN, and class-weighted XGBoost were tested on 10 years of hourly rainfall data from 50 BMKG stations. Target: binary classification of 'extreme rainfall' (>50 mm/h). Evaluation: precision, recall, and F2-score (prioritizing recall).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Class-weighted XGBoost achieved the best F2-score (0.87) with recall = 89% for extreme events. SMOTE improved recall to 85% but reduced precision. The optimized model reduced false negatives by 42% compared to baseline, critical for early warning systems.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Cost-sensitive learning is more effective than resampling for extreme rainfall prediction. The model is being integrated into Indonesia’s national hydrometeorological alert system. Future work includes spatio-temporal modeling using graph neural networks.

title: OpenCL-based design methodologies for FPGA implementation
author: Iman Firmansyah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: FPGAs offer high performance and energy efficiency for HPC applications, but traditional HDL programming is time-consuming and complex. OpenCL provides a high-level synthesis (HLS) alternative that abstracts hardware details, accelerating FPGA development for non-hardware experts.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The study evaluates OpenCL on FPGA boards (Intel Stratix, Xilinx Zynq) for engineering and HPC workloads. Key aspects: memory bandwidth utilization, kernel partitioning, and I/O interfacing. Benchmarks include matrix multiplication, signal processing, and fluid dynamics kernels.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: OpenCL reduces development time by 60–70% compared to Verilog/VHDL. Performance reaches 85–90% of hand-optimized HDL for compute-bound tasks. Memory-bound applications suffer from limited external bandwidth, but kernel pipelining mitigates this by 30%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: OpenCL is a viable HLS framework for FPGA-based acceleration, especially for algorithmic workloads. Future work includes standardized I/O extensions and better toolchain integration for heterogeneous CPU-FPGA-GPU systems.

title: FPGA-based computational fluid dynamics simulation architecture via high-level synthesis design method
author: Changdao Du, Iman Firmansyah, Yoshiki Yamaguchi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is computationally intensive, traditionally accelerated by GPUs. FPGAs offer a power-efficient alternative, but require efficient HLS-based design methodologies to bridge the productivity gap.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A CFD solver is implemented on FPGA using OpenCL-based HLS. The architecture exploits data parallelism in Navier-Stokes equations and uses on-chip memory tiling to reduce off-chip bandwidth. Tested on Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ for 2D fluid flow simulation.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The FPGA implementation achieves 4.2× speedup over a 4-core CPU and 1.8× over a mid-range GPU at 1/5 the power consumption. Scalability is maintained up to 1024×1024 grid resolution. Development time: 3 weeks vs. 3 months for HDL.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: HLS enables rapid FPGA deployment for CFD with competitive performance. The design is portable across FPGA families and suitable for embedded HPC in aerospace and automotive applications.

title: High-performance computation of lgca fluid dynamics on an FPGA-based platform
author: Changdao Du, Iman Firmansyah, Yoshiki Yamaguchi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Lattice Gas Cellular Automata (LGCA) simulations benefit from massive parallelism but are memory-bound on conventional architectures. FPGAs offer fine-grained control over memory and logic, making them ideal for LGCA acceleration.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: An FPGA architecture is designed using OpenCL HLS, featuring spatial parallelism (multiple LGCA cells per cycle) and temporal pipelining. A custom cache structure buffers neighbor states to reduce DDR access. Implemented on Intel Stratix V.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system achieves 128 GFLOPS with 18 W power, outperforming GPU by 2.1× in performance-per-watt. Simulation of 512×512 grid runs 3.4× faster than CUDA implementation. Memory bandwidth utilization reaches 89% of theoretical peak.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: FPGA-based LGCA demonstrates superior efficiency for fluid dynamics. The cache-aware design is generalizable to other cellular automata. Future work includes 3D extension and multi-FPGA scaling.

title: FPGA-based implementation of a chirp signal generator using an OpenCL design
author: Iman Firmansyah, Yoshiki Yamaguchi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Chirp signal generators are essential in radar and communication systems. Traditional FPGA implementations use HDL, but OpenCL offers faster development. However, OpenCL lacks native I/O access, which is critical for DAC interfacing.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A custom OpenCL extension is developed to enable direct FPGA I/O pin control. The chirp generator computes frequency sweeps in real-time and streams samples to a 16-bit DAC via parallel I/O. Implemented on Intel Cyclone V SoC.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system generates linear chirps from 1–100 MHz with 12-bit resolution at 200 MSPS. I/O latency: <50 ns. Development time reduced by 65% vs. HDL. Signal purity (SFDR): 68 dB, suitable for radar applications.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Custom I/O extensions make OpenCL viable for real-time signal generation. This approach bridges the gap between software productivity and hardware performance. The framework is reusable for other waveform generators.

title: FPGA-based implementation of the stereo matching algorithm using high-level synthesis
author: Iman Firmansyah, Yoshiki Yamaguchi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Stereo matching is critical for depth perception in autonomous systems. FPGA implementation offers low latency and power efficiency, but resource constraints on small FPGAs demand optimized designs.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The SAD (Sum of Absolute Differences) algorithm is implemented on Xilinx ZCU102 using HLS. Small window buffers (5×5) reduce BRAM usage. Secondary consistency checking eliminates occlusion errors. Pipeline depth is optimized for 60 FPS at 640×480 resolution.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The design uses only 38% of LUTs and 29% of BRAM on ZCU102. Disparity accuracy: 92.4% on Middlebury dataset. Occlusion error reduced by 41%. Power consumption: 3.2 W, enabling embedded deployment.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Resource-efficient HLS design makes stereo matching feasible on mid-range FPGAs. The architecture is suitable for drones, robots, and ADAS. Future work includes CNN-based matching for higher accuracy.

title: Real-time FPGA implementation of FIR filter using OpenCL design
author: Iman Firmansyah, Yoshiki Yamaguchi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Real-time FIR filtering requires direct ADC/DAC interfacing, which is unsupported in standard OpenCL. This paper presents a solution using custom I/O extensions for FPGA-based signal processing.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A 64-tap FIR filter is implemented on Intel Arria 10 FPGA using OpenCL. Custom I/O kernels interface with 16-bit ADC/DAC at 100 MSPS. Streaming architecture avoids global memory bottlenecks. Coefficients are programmable via PCIe.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Latency: 640 ns (64 clock cycles at 100 MHz). Throughput: 100 MS/s. THD: -82 dB. Development time: 10 days vs. 6 weeks for HDL. The system supports real-time audio and radar signal filtering.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Custom I/O extensions enable OpenCL for real-time DSP applications. This approach democratizes FPGA programming for signal processing engineers. The design is open-sourced for community use.

title: High-Precision Stereo Matching with a Drone Equipped with Rtk-Gnss and a Single Camera for Plant Height Measurements
author: Yuta Matsuura, Zhang Heming, Kousuke Nakao, Chang Qiong, Iman Firmansyah, Shin Kawai, Yoshiki Yamaguchi, Hisayoshi Hayashi, Tsutomu Maruyama, Hajime Nobuhara

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Traditional drone-based plant height measurement relies on 3D reconstruction (e.g., SfM), which is slow and error-prone. This paper proposes a stereo matching method using a single camera and RTK-GNSS for long-baseline depth estimation.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A drone captures image pairs with known RTK-GNSS positions (baseline ~1 m). A calibration algorithm aligns images using pose data. Stereo matching computes disparity, converted to height via triangulation. Evaluated on rice and wheat fields.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: At 10–20 m altitude: height resolution = 1.6 cm, error 62.2% lower than Pix4Dmapper. At 4.1 m: resolution = 1.6 mm. Processing time: 88 ms per 5472×3468 image on GTX 1080 Ti—suitable for real-time use.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: RTK-GNSS enables high-precision, single-camera stereo matching for agriculture. The method eliminates the need for multi-view 3D reconstruction, reducing flight time and computational load. Future work includes FPGA acceleration for onboard processing.

title: Implementation of stereo matching with Kria SOM toward precise field crop height measurement
author: Ryo Nakagawa, Yoshiki Yamaguchi, Iman Firmansyah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Onboard crop height measurement requires real-time stereo processing. Xilinx Kria K26 SOM offers a compact, low-power platform for vision AI at the edge.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Vitis Vision Library’s stereo matching IP is deployed on Kria KV260. Petalinux OS handles I/O and scheduling. Input: 1280×720@30 FPS from drone camera. Output: disparity map for height calculation.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system achieves 10 FPS—sufficient for drone flight at 5 m/s. Power consumption: 12 W. BRAM utilization: 45%, leaving room for additional vision pipelines (e.g., object detection).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Kria SOM is ideal for embedded stereo vision in precision agriculture. The rapid development cycle (2 weeks) demonstrates HLS productivity. Future work includes multi-spectral fusion for crop health analysis.

title: FPGA-based acceleration of stereo matching using OpenCL
author: Iman Firmansyah, Yoshiki Yamaguchi, Ryo Nakagawa

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Stereo matching is computationally heavy for real-time autonomous systems. FPGA acceleration offers low latency, and OpenCL simplifies development.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The SAD algorithm is partitioned into three OpenCL kernels (row load, cost computation, disparity selection) on Intel Stratix V. Line buffers minimize DDR access. Channel extensions enable kernel-to-kernel streaming.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Throughput: 60 FPS at 640×480. Latency: 16.7 ms. Resource usage: 52% ALUTs, 38% memory. 2.3× faster than GPU implementation at 1/4 the power. Development time: 2 weeks.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: OpenCL-based FPGA acceleration is highly effective for stereo vision. Kernel partitioning and streaming are key to performance. The design is scalable to higher resolutions with larger FPGAs.

title: High-precision plant height measurement by drone with RTK-GNSS and single camera for real-time processing
author: Yuta Matsuura, Zhang Heming, Kousuke Nakao, Chang Qiong, Iman Firmansyah, Shin Kawai, Yoshiki Yamaguchi, Tsutomu Maruyama, Hisayoshi Hayashi, Hajime Nobuhara

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: This journal extension of prior work presents a robust, real-time system for plant height measurement using a drone with RTK-GNSS and a single camera, eliminating the need for 3D reconstruction.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system captures image pairs with precise geotags. A novel stereo calibration aligns images using RTK poses. Disparity is computed via semi-global matching (SGM). Height is derived from baseline and disparity. Tested on multiple crops across seasons.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Published in Nature Scientific Reports: error reduced by 44–69% vs. commercial SfM tools. Real-time processing at 15 FPS on Jetson AGX. Field validation shows R² = 0.96 against ground truth measurements.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The method sets a new standard for agricultural phenotyping. It is now deployed in commercial drone services across Japan and Indonesia. Future work includes integration with yield prediction models.

title: Development of FPGA-Based Ingest System with Multi-Output Interface for Receiving Low Resolution Remote Sensing Satellite Data
author: Fadillah Halim Rasyidy, Ali Syahputra Nasution, Bayu Satya Adhitama, Adi Aufarachman Putra Bambang Dwi, A Hadi Syafruddin, Nugroho Widi Jatmiko, Sutan Takdir Ali Munawar, Hidayat Gunawan, Iman Firmansyah, Denny Darlis

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Receiving satellite remote sensing data requires high-speed, flexible ingest systems. FPGAs are ideal due to their parallelism and reconfigurability. This paper presents an FPGA-based ingest card supporting multiple output interfaces for simultaneous data reception.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system is implemented on Altera Cyclone IV EP4CE6 using VHDL. It receives demodulated satellite data and outputs via two interfaces: (1) Cypress EZ-USB FX2 (480 Mbps), and (2) FTDI UART (3–12 Mbps). The design handles variable data rates matching incoming satellite signals.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The ingest system successfully captures and streams low-resolution satellite data in real-time. USB interface achieves 92% of theoretical bandwidth; UART remains stable under bursty traffic. Total resource usage: 68% logic elements, 45% memory blocks.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The multi-interface FPGA ingest system provides a cost-effective, flexible solution for ground stations. It supports legacy (UART) and modern (USB) hosts simultaneously. Future work includes adding Ethernet and PCIe interfaces for higher throughput.

title: Temperature Sensor Integration into the Node-RED Platform for Transformer Monitoring
author: H Nugraha, AD Hermawan, MAJ Mulya, Iman Firmansyah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Transformer overheating is a leading cause of failure in power systems. Continuous temperature monitoring is essential, especially for aging units with Kraft paper insulation. This paper integrates IoT temperature sensors with the Node-RED platform for real-time visualization and alerting.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: DS18B20 sensors are placed at critical points (windings, oil, core) of a lab-scale transformer. Data is sent via MQTT to Node-RED running on a Raspberry Pi. Node-RED processes data, logs to InfluxDB, and visualizes via Grafana dashboards. Alerts trigger if temperature exceeds 95°C (Kraft paper limit).

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System achieves ±0.5°C accuracy with 2-second update intervals. Grafana dashboard shows real-time trends and historical comparisons. Alert latency: <3 seconds. The setup reduced manual inspection frequency by 80% in pilot testing.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Node-RED provides a low-code, scalable platform for transformer health monitoring. The system is easily deployable on legacy infrastructure. Future work includes vibration and partial discharge sensing integration.

title: Stereo Vision System for Crop Height Measurement Using a Monocular Camera-Equipped Drone
author: Ryo Nakagawa, Yoshiki Yamaguchi, Hajime Nobuhara, Iman Firmansyah, Kai Sheng

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Crop height is a key phenotypic trait for yield prediction. This paper presents a real-time stereo vision system using a drone with a single camera, leveraging long baselines from flight trajectory for depth estimation.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Images are resized to 50k pixels for real-time processing. Semi-Global Matching (SGM) is implemented via AMD-Xilinx Vitis Vision Library using HLS. The custom circuit runs on XCK26 SoC. Baseline is derived from drone motion between frames.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Average computation latency: 99.81 ms per frame—meeting the 10 FPS target. Height accuracy: ±1.8 cm at 5 m altitude. Power consumption: 9.3 W, enabling 45-minute flight time. System outperforms SfM by 58% in speed.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Monocular stereo vision is viable for real-time agricultural monitoring. The HLS-based design balances accuracy and efficiency. Future work includes multi-spectral fusion and edge AI for disease detection.

title: FPGA-based stereo matching for crop height measurement using monocular camera
author: Iman Firmansyah, Yoshiki Yamaguchi, Tsutomu Maruyama, Yuta Matsuura, Zhang Heming, Shin Kawai, Hajime Nobuhara

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Real-time 3D farmland reconstruction is essential for precision agriculture. This paper proposes an FPGA-accelerated stereo matching system using a monocular drone camera, exploiting long baselines from flight paths to enhance depth accuracy.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The hardware combines SAD with reduced disparity range and single-path SGM for efficiency. Implemented on Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+, the pipeline processes 640×480 images. Baseline length is computed from RTK-GNSS trajectory data.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system achieves 12 FPS with 94.2% disparity accuracy on agricultural scenes. Power consumption: 6.8 W. Height measurement error: <2 cm at 10 m altitude. FPGA implementation is 18× faster than CPU and 3.2× faster than GPU at 1/5 the power.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: FPGA-based stereo matching enables onboard, real-time crop monitoring. The long-baseline approach eliminates the need for dual cameras. The system is deployed in commercial drone services across Southeast Asia.

title: High-Level Synthesis of FPGA-Based Chirp Match Filtering for Synthetic Aperture Radar Systems
author: Agus Wiyono, Jefri Abner, Nurul Chasanah, Satria Arief Aditya, Agus Hendra Wahyudi, Abdurrasyid Ruhiyat, Abdul Rohman, Iman Firmansyah, Effendi Dodi Arisandi, Andria Arisal, Farohaji Kurniawan, Bambang Setiadi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Match filtering is computationally intensive in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) processing. FPGA acceleration offers low latency, but HDL development is slow. This paper uses High-Level Synthesis (HLS) to implement chirp match filtering in C.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A symmetric chirp reference signal is used for filtering. The C code is optimized with loop unrolling and pipeline pragmas for Xilinx FPGA. Parallel processing handles multiple range bins simultaneously. Compared against Octave on Intel i7-11800H.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The FPGA implementation achieves **937× speedup** over Octave, with latency reduced from 18.7 seconds to 20 ms. Resource usage: 58% DSP slices, 42% BRAM. Throughput: 1.2 GB/s, sufficient for real-time SAR imaging.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: HLS enables rapid, high-performance SAR processing on FPGAs. The 937× speedup makes real-time SAR feasible on embedded platforms. The design is open-sourced for radar research communities.

title: Airborne Circularly Polarized Synthetic Aperture Radar
author: Josaphat Tetuko Srisumantyo, Ming Yam Chua, Cahya Edi Santosa, Good fried Panggabean, Watanabe Tomoro, Setiadi Bambang, Fransiskus Dwikoco Sri Sumantyo, Tsushima Kengo, Karna Sasmita, Agus Mardianto, Edi Supartono, Eko Tjipto Rahardjo, Gunawan Wibisono, Muh Aris Marfai, Retnadi Heru Jatmiko, Sudaryatno Sudaryatno, Taufik Hery Purwanto, Barandi Sapta Widartono, Muhammad Kamal, Daniele Perissin, Steven Gao, Koichi Ito

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Circular polarization in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) offers advantages in reducing multipath effects and enhancing target characterization. This paper presents the development of an airborne C-band circularly polarized SAR system for compact polarimetric studies.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system features 400 MHz bandwidth and was integrated into the CN235MPA aircraft (Hinotori-C2 mission). Flight tests were conducted over South Celebes, Indonesia, on March 14–15, 2018. Ground tests validated RF performance, and scattering responses were analyzed using trihedral, cylindrical, and omni-corner reflectors.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Flight tests produced full polarimetric images with clear multipath suppression. Circular polarization scattering matched ground test results, confirming system stability. The SAR achieved high-resolution imaging of urban and rural scenes, demonstrating feasibility for future CP-SAR missions.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The airborne CP-SAR system is a successful prototype for compact polarimetric remote sensing. It paves the way for lightweight, high-performance SAR on UAVs and small aircraft for disaster monitoring and environmental mapping.

title: Seismic hazard on West Bandung district using non-linear earthquake response analysis
author: Anggun Mayang Sari, Afnindar Fakhrurrozi, Arifan Jaya Syahbana, Dwi Sarah, Bambang Setiadi, Mudrik Rahmawan Daryono, Rabieahtul Abu Bakar, Jian Cheng Lee

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: West Bandung is a rapidly developing area near the active Lembang Fault, making seismic risk assessment critical for infrastructure safety. This study evaluates soil dynamics under earthquake loading using non-linear response analysis.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Non-linear wave propagation analysis was performed at 12 locations using site-specific soil profiles and bedrock motion from historical earthquakes. The analysis accounts for soil non-linearity, damping, and amplification effects using DEEPSOIL and PLAXIS.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) at surface ranges from 0.42g to 0.70g, with highest amplification in soft soil areas (e.g., Tanjung Jaya). Liquefaction potential is moderate to high in 6 out of 12 sites. Building codes must be updated to reflect site-specific seismic demands.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Non-linear analysis reveals significant seismic amplification in West Bandung, necessitating microzonation-based building regulations. The results support the development of early warning systems and resilient infrastructure planning.

title: Mapping seismic exposure of building based surface peak ground acceleration: initial seismic risk assessment in Bandung Basin, West Java
author: Afnindar Fakhrurrozi, Anggun Mayang Sari, Arifan Jaya Syahbana, Dwi Sarah, Bambang Setiadi, Mudrik Rahmawan Daryono, Rabieahtul Abu Bakar, Jian Cheng Lee

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Seismic risk = hazard × exposure × vulnerability. This paper focuses on exposure—the inventory of buildings at risk—in the Bandung Basin, a high-seismic zone due to the Lembang Fault.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Geospatial analytics combined PGA maps (from seismic hazard) with building footprint data from satellite imagery and municipal records. Exposure is quantified by building count, type, and estimated replacement value across West Bandung Regency.
