sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Over 120,000 buildings are exposed to PGA >0.5g. High-exposure zones correlate with dense residential areas near fault lines. Economic exposure exceeds IDR 42 trillion. Older masonry structures dominate high-risk zones, increasing potential loss.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: This exposure map is foundational for seismic risk modeling and insurance. It enables targeted retrofitting programs and land-use planning to reduce future losses in the Bandung Basin.

title: Deformation analysis for Padang earthquake using GPS data
author: Rahmat Iqbal, D Arisa, B Setiadi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The 2009 Mw 7.6 Padang earthquake caused significant crustal deformation. This study analyzes surface displacement using GPS data from the Sumatran GPS Array (SuGAr).

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: GPS data from 4 stations (TIKU, PSKI, NGNG, MSAI) were processed using GAMIT/GLOBK for 100 days before and after the event. Daily positions were computed to track co-seismic displacement vectors.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Mentawai stations (MSAI, NGNG) moved 38–50 mm southwest; mainland stations (TIKU, PSKI) shifted 5–12 mm northwest. The pattern confirms thrust faulting with uplift in Mentawai and subsidence on Sumatra’s west coast.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: GPS data provide critical validation for seismic models. The observed deformation aligns with elastic dislocation theory, supporting future hazard assessments for the Mentawai seismic gap.

title: Pre-and Coseismic Analysis of the Mw7.6 Padang Earthquake 2009 from Geodetic Approach
author: D Arisa, B Setiadi, WS Priyanto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Understanding pre- and co-seismic deformation is key to earthquake cycle modeling. This paper presents a comprehensive geodetic analysis of the 2009 Padang earthquake using the full SuGAr network.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Data from 12 deformed GPS stations across Sumatra were processed using GAMIT/GLOBK with DGPS technique. Time series from 2009 reveal interseismic strain accumulation and co-seismic slip.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Pre-seismic strain rate: 45–60 mm/year. Co-seismic offsets: 8–50 mm southwest in Mentawai, 3–15 mm northwest on mainland. Post-seismic relaxation continues for months, indicating viscoelastic mantle response.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The geodetic record captures the full earthquake cycle, improving slip distribution models. Results inform tsunami early warning systems and long-term seismic hazard forecasts for western Sumatra.

title: SEISMIC WAVE PROPAGATION IN BANDUNG BASIN, WEST JAVA
author: Anggun Mayang Sari, Afnindar Fakhrurrozi, Arifan Jaya Syahbana, Dwi Sarah, Mudrik Rahmawan Daryono, Bambang Setiadi, Rabieahtul Abu Bakar

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Bandung Basin’s soft sediments amplify seismic waves, increasing earthquake risk. This study models wave propagation to quantify surface ground motion.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Non-linear seismic response analysis is applied using 1D soil columns and bedrock motion from regional faults. PGA is computed at the surface for multiple scenarios using SHAKE2000.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: PGA ranges from 0.42g (Ciwastra) to 0.70g (Tanjung Jaya), exceeding design spectra in Indonesian codes. Amplification is highest in areas with thick clay layers and high water tables.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Site effects dominate seismic risk in Bandung Basin. Microzonation maps based on this study are recommended for urban planning and critical infrastructure design.

title: Disturbance observer-based attitude control of the air-bearing platform using a reaction wheel
author: Harry Septanto, Farohaji Kurniawan, Bambang Setiadi, Edi Kurniawan, Djoko Suprijanto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Reaction wheels are key actuators for spacecraft attitude control but suffer from motor disturbances. This paper proposes a disturbance observer (DOB) to enhance control precision on an air-bearing platform.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A linear DOB is integrated with a PID controller. The air-bearing platform simulates microgravity. Performance is evaluated via ISE, IAE, ITAE, and control effort metrics under step and disturbance inputs.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The DOB-based controller reduces ISE by 42%, IAE by 38%, and control effort by 29% compared to PID alone. It effectively rejects harmonic and step disturbances, achieving steady-state error <0.05°.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: DOB significantly improves attitude control robustness. The design is scalable to real satellites and UAVs. Future work includes adaptive DOB for time-varying disturbances.

title: Circularly Polarized Antenna Array 1×7 Fed by Power Weighting Distribution
author: Farohaji Kurniawan, Dewi Anggraeni, Satria A Aditya, Nurul L Muzayadah, Gunawan S Prabowo, Harry Septanto, Bambang Setiadi, Peberlin Sitompul, Joko Widodo, Yuta Izumi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Circularly polarized (CP) antenna arrays are essential for satellite and radar systems to mitigate polarization mismatch. This paper presents a 7-element CP array with sidelobe suppression.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Each patch is modified with a square ring slot and 45° truncations for CP. A power weighting distribution feeds the array to reduce sidelobes. Simulated and measured at 9.4 GHz using vector network analyzer.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Axial ratio <3 dB over 0.8 GHz bandwidth. Sidelobe level: -15.1 dB. Reflection coefficient < -10 dB over 1 GHz. Radiation pattern shows symmetric CP with 12.3 dBi gain.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The power-weighted CP array achieves excellent polarization purity and low sidelobes, suitable for X-band SAR and communication payloads on drones and small satellites.

title: Performance Analysis of Carbon Composite Materials with VARI Method for Electromagnetic Interference Applications
author: Nurul Lailatul Muzayadah, Dewi Nur Anggraeni, Satria Arief Aditya, Nurul Chasanah, Farohaji Kurniawan, Agus Hendra Wahyudi, Yanuar Prabowo, Cahya Edi Santosa, Jefri Abner Hamonangan, Bambang Setiadi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) can disrupt SAR systems on drones. This study evaluates carbon composite shielding using the Vacuum Assisted Resin Infusion (VARI) method.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Carbon fiber composites were fabricated via VARI. S-parameters (S11, S21) were measured in an anechoic chamber from 0.9–5.3 GHz using a VNA. Shielding effectiveness (SE) was computed from reflection and transmission losses.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: SE exceeds 30 dB across the band, sufficient to protect SAR electronics. Reflection loss dominates at lower frequencies; absorption increases with frequency. Material is lightweight (<1.8 g/cm³) and structurally robust.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: VARI-based carbon composites are ideal for EMI shielding in aerospace applications. They integrate structural and electromagnetic functions, reducing drone payload weight and complexity.

title: Pemodelan Banjir Rob Wilayah Jakarta Utara Menggunakan Sistem Informasi Geografis
author: Indah Ferdiani Zuhriah, Bambang Setiadi, Seftiawan Samsu Rijal

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: North Jakarta faces increasing tidal flooding (rob) due to sea-level rise and land subsidence. This study models inundation extent under various tidal scenarios using GIS.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Digital elevation model (DEM) is combined with Mean Sea Level (MSL) and Higher High Water Level (HHWL) data. Inundation maps are generated for 0.4 m to 1.96 m scenarios using ArcGIS Spatial Analyst.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: At 0.4 m: 54 ha residential, 59 ha buildings, 146 ha agriculture affected. At 1.96 m: 983 ha residential, 493 ha buildings, 830 ha agriculture flooded. Penjaringan, Cilincing, Pademangan, and Tanjung Priok are most vulnerable.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: GIS-based modeling provides actionable data for disaster mitigation. Results support the need for sea walls, elevated infrastructure, and managed retreat in high-risk zones of North Jakarta.

title: Directivity of coseismic ionospheric disturbances propagation following the 2016 West Sumatra earthquake using three-dimensional tomography GNSS-TEC
author: Mokhamad Nur Cahyadi, Deasy Arisa, Ihsan Naufal Muafiry, Buldan Muslim, Ririn Wuri Rahayu, Meilfan Eka Putra, Mega Wulansari, Bambang Setiadi, Andria Arisal, Pakhrur Razi, Syachrul Arief

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Earthquakes generate ionospheric disturbances detectable via GNSS-TEC. This paper uses 3D tomography to analyze the direction and evolution of coseismic ionospheric disturbances (CID) from the 2016 West Sumatra quake.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: TEC data from 50+ GNSS stations in Sumatra and Java are inverted into a 3D electron density model (1°×1.2°×75 km). Continuity constraints stabilize the solution. Checkerboard tests validate resolution.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: CID appears at 300 km altitude 11 min post-quake, with max amplitude 2.9 TECU. It propagates 1° per minute along the geomagnetic field. Anomaly weakens after 8 min. Speed: 1–1.72 km/s, consistent with acoustic-gravity waves.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: 3D tomography reveals the anisotropic propagation of CID, governed by geomagnetic field geometry. This improves ionospheric earthquake early warning and space weather modeling.

title: Perancangan Dashboard Perangkat Through the Wall Radar Imaging (TWRI) untuk Pencarian Korban Reruntuhan Bangunan
author: Satria Arief Aditya, Abdul Rohman, Bambang Setiadi, Nuha Nadhiroh

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Pencarian korban hidup di bawah reruntuhan memerlukan teknologi non-invasif. Through-the-Wall Radar Imaging (TWRI) mendeteksi gerakan pernapasan sebagai indikator kehidupan. Penelitian ini merancang dashboard pemantauan berbasis LabVIEW untuk sistem TWRI yang diintegrasikan dengan drone.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sistem menggunakan radar FMCW yang disimulasikan untuk drone multirotor. Data radar diproses dan divisualisasikan melalui antarmuka LabVIEW pada laptop (RAM 32 GB). Dashboard dirancang untuk menampilkan sinyal pernapasan secara real-time dengan template yang dapat dikembangkan menjadi aplikasi mandiri.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Dashboard berhasil menampilkan simulasi sinyal pernapasan dengan resolusi waktu 0.1 detik. Antarmuka intuitif memungkinkan operator mengidentifikasi korban dalam 3 detik. Sistem siap untuk integrasi dengan perangkat keras radar fisik pada tahap berikutnya.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Desain dashboard berbasis LabVIEW memberikan fondasi kuat untuk sistem TWRI operasional. Pengembangan selanjutnya mencakup kompresi data real-time dan notifikasi otomatis saat deteksi positif.

title: Seismic hazard analysis on Solok Regency, West Sumatra to support local government development program
author: Anggun Mayang Sari, Afnindar Fakhrurrozi, Andria Arisal, Bambang Setiadi, Hendri Gusti Putra, Nafri Nafri, Rabieahtul Abu Bakar, Zamri Ramli

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Solok Regency, West Sumatra, is highly vulnerable to earthquakes due to its proximity to the Sumatran Fault. This study conducts Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Analysis (PSHA) to support resilient infrastructure planning.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: PSHA is performed for a 2475-year return period, considering seismic sources within 500 km of Arosuka. Ground motion models and fault parameters are integrated to compute Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) at bedrock.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: PGA at bedrock reaches 1.0g in high-risk zones. Urban centers like Solok City show PGA >0.7g, exceeding current building code requirements. Results are mapped to guide zoning and critical facility placement.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The PSHA map is a critical input for Solok’s disaster-resilient development. It mandates seismic retrofitting of hospitals, schools, and government buildings. Future work includes site amplification analysis for surface PGA.

title: Implementation of Backprojection Algorithm for Synthetic Aperture Radar Image Processing on Low-Cost Hardware Platform
author: Agus Wiyono, Nurul Chasanah, Jefri Abner Hamonangan, Abdurrasyid Ruhiyat, Abdul Rohman, Farohaji Kurniawan, Satria Arief Aditya, Agus Hendra Wahyudi, Novelita Rahayu, Andria Arisal, Bambang Setiadi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: SAR image processing is computationally intensive, typically requiring high-end workstations. This paper explores the feasibility of running the Backprojection Algorithm (BPA) on affordable Raspberry Pi platforms.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: BPA is implemented in GNU Octave on Raspberry Pi 3B and 4. A single-threaded baseline is compared against a parallelized version using Octave’s parallel package. Performance is measured in processing time per SAR image.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Single-threaded execution is too slow (>1 hour/image). Parallelized BPA on Pi 4 reduces time to 18 minutes—viable for near-real-time applications in resource-limited settings. Memory usage stays below 2.5 GB.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Raspberry Pi can serve as a low-cost SAR processing node for educational and field deployments. Future work includes FPGA acceleration and integration with drone-based SAR systems.

title: Implementing Satellite-borne Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging Algorithm with Open Source Scientific Software
author: Bambang Setiadi, Andria Arisal, Afnindar Fakhrurrozi, Harry Septanto, Farohaji Kurniawan, Satria Arief Aditya

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Satellite SAR imaging requires complex algorithms, often implemented in C/C++. This paper demonstrates the Range Doppler Algorithm (RDA) using GNU Octave for academic and prototyping purposes.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: RDA is implemented in four steps: (1) range compression, (2) secondary range compression, (3) azimuth compression, and (4) image formation. Raw satellite SAR data is processed into single-look complex (SLC) images.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The Octave implementation produces SLC images comparable to commercial software, with 92% correlation in pixel intensity. Processing time: 22 minutes for a 10,000×10,000 pixel scene on a standard laptop.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: GNU Octave is a viable tool for SAR algorithm development in research environments. Its open-source nature lowers entry barriers for students and researchers in developing countries.

title: Deformation Monitoring of Sipora Island Using Geodetic Global Positioning System Data
author: Reno Fadilah, Pakhrur Razi, Bambang Setiadi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Sipora Island lies in the Mentawai seismic gap, capable of generating Mw >8.9 earthquakes. Continuous deformation monitoring is essential for early warning.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: One year of GPS data (2019) from 5 SuGAr stations on Sipora and 16 global IGS stations are processed using GAMIT/GLOBK. Daily positions are analyzed to compute velocity vectors.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Sipora Island moves northeast at 62 mm/year—consistent with Indo-Australian Plate motion. No significant strain accumulation was detected in 2019, but long-term monitoring remains critical.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: GPS provides reliable deformation monitoring in the Mentawai Islands. The data feed into Indonesia’s national seismic hazard model and tsunami early warning system.

title: Experimental evaluation of polarimetric ground based synthetic aperture radar imaging using portable vna
author: Nurul Chasanah, Jefri Abner, Agus Wiyono, Novelita Rahayu, Farohaji Kurniawan, Wahyu Widada, Bambang Setiadi, Dadang Gunawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Polarimetric GBSAR enables material classification and target identification. This study evaluates a portable VNA-based GBSAR system for remote sensing applications.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A two-port VNA and horn antennas are used in stop-and-go stripmap mode. Targets: 4 corner reflectors and 2 UAVs. Data is processed using Back-Projection Algorithm (BPA) in an indoor controlled environment.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system achieves 0.5 m resolution at 5.3 GHz. Polarimetric signatures distinguish metallic (CR) from composite (UAV) targets. Co-polarized channels show 12 dB higher SNR than cross-polarized.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Portable VNA-based GBSAR is feasible for field deployment. It provides a low-cost entry point for polarimetric SAR research in Indonesia. Future work includes outdoor validation and motion compensation.

title: Automatic pulse duration of chirp generation for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) depend on altitude changes of the aircraft
author: Agus Wiyono, Bambang Setiadi, Satria Arief Aditya, Farohaji Kurniawan, Harry Septanto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: SAR image quality depends on signal density, which varies with aircraft altitude. This paper proposes an automatic chirp pulse duration adjustment system based on real-time altitude data.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Chirp signals are generated via DDS with 14-bit DAC and 200 MHz sampling. Pulse duration is dynamically adjusted from 1–1500 m altitude to maintain optimal signal density. Simulated using MATLAB and GNU Radio.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The system maintains constant signal density across altitudes, improving image SNR by 8–12 dB compared to fixed pulse duration. Latency for adjustment: <50 ms—suitable for real-time flight.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Automatic pulse duration control enhances SAR adaptability to variable flight conditions. The system is ready for integration with BRIN’s airborne SAR platform.

title: Design and implementation of an integrated data processing unit with range matched filtering for lab scale synthetic aperture radar sensor
author: Jefri Abner Hamonangan, Bambang Setiadi, Farohaji Kurniawan, Agus Wiyono, Wahyu Widada, Nurul Chasanah, Abdul Rohman, Agus Hendra Wahyudi, Abdurrasyid Ruhiyat, Novelita Rahayu, Satria Arief Aditya

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: BRIN is developing a lab-scale SAR system for MALE UAVs. This paper presents the integrated Data Acquisition Unit (DAU) and Data Processing Unit (DPU) with real-time matched filtering.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system uses 5.3 GHz chirp with 150 MHz bandwidth (1 m range resolution). DAU samples IQ baseband at 200 MSPS. DPU performs range compression via matched filtering before storage.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Integrated DAU-DPU reduces data volume by 60% through on-the-fly compression. End-to-end latency: 120 ms. The system successfully images targets at 50 m range in lab tests.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Hardware-software co-design enables efficient SAR data handling. The lab prototype validates the architecture for future airborne deployment.

title: Design of LO Phase Shifter Based on Quadrature Hybrid Ring Coupler for IQ Mixer in Synthetic Aperture Radar Applications
author: Abdurrasyid Ruhiyat, Farohaji Kurniawan, Bambang Setiadi, Catur Apriono

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: IQ mixers require precise 90° phase shift for image rejection in SAR transceivers. This paper presents a quadrature hybrid ring coupler as a passive LO phase shifter.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The coupler is designed for 5.3 GHz and fabricated on Rogers substrate. S-parameters are measured using VNA. Performance is evaluated by integration with an IQ mixer in a SAR RF chain.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Measured S11 = -33.85 dB, isolation = -29.56 dB, insertion loss <0.8 dB. Phase difference between outputs: 90.2° ±1.5° over 500 MHz bandwidth—excellent for SAR applications.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The hybrid coupler provides a robust, low-cost phase shifting solution for SAR IQ mixers. It enhances bandwidth and image rejection without active components.

title: Light weight dual polarized horn antenna for polarimetry C-band synthetic aperture radar sensor onboard UAV
author: Agus Hendra Wahyudi, Farohaji Kurniawan, Bambang Setiadi, Agus Wiyono, Satria Arief Aditya, Wahyu Widada, Effendi Dodi Arisandi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: UAVs require lightweight, high-performance antennas for polarimetric SAR. This paper presents a dual circularly polarized horn antenna for C-band UAV-SAR.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A pyramid horn with three-stepped septum polarizer and dual coaxial feeds is designed in CST. It alternately generates RHCP and LHCP. Fabricated and tested in anechoic chamber.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: S11/S22 < -10 dB from 4–6.7 GHz. Axial ratio <3 dB from 4.4–6.4 GHz. Gain: 15 dBiC, beamwidth: 28°. Total weight: 420 g—suitable for small UAVs.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The antenna enables full polarimetric SAR on UAVs with minimal payload impact. It is now integrated into BRIN’s MALE UAV SAR payload for environmental monitoring.

title: Polarimetric Calibration for Ground-based Synthetic Aperture Radar based on Point Target Approach
author: Nurul Chasanah, Dadang Gunawan, Farohaji Kurniawan, Agus Wiyono, Jefri Abner, Bambang Setiadi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Polarimetric calibration (PolCal) is essential for quantitative GBSAR analysis. This paper presents an external calibration method using point targets for C-band SFCW radar.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: One trihedral and two dihedral corner reflectors with different tilt angles are used. Calibration corrects channel imbalance between co-pol and cross-pol channels in a VNA-based SFCW GBSAR system.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: After calibration, channel imbalance is reduced from 4.2 dB to 0.3 dB. Polarimetric signatures of natural targets (trees, buildings) show improved consistency. Calibration stability: ±0.1 dB over 24 hours.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The point-target approach provides accurate, repeatable PolCal for GBSAR. It enables reliable change detection and material classification in landslide and deformation monitoring.

title: Analysis of alternatives methodology for large-scale information system implementation
author: Andria Arisal, Bambang Setiadi, Ichwanul Muslim

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Indonesia’s SPBE (Electronic-Based Government System) policy mandates integrated digital services, yet fragmented implementations persist. This paper proposes a structured methodology to evaluate alternatives for large-scale information system deployment, focusing on cost, benefit, and risk.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The framework quantifies alternatives using multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA). Applied to SP4N-LAPOR!—the national public complaint system—stakeholders evaluate options: (1) adopt national system, (2) integrate with local system, or (3) develop custom solution. Metrics include TCO, interoperability score, and security risk.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: The methodology enabled quantitative comparison: national adoption scored highest in interoperability (92/100) and lowest TCO (IDR 1.2B vs. IDR 3.8B for custom). Risk of data silos dropped by 76% under the national option. The approach is now adopted by 3 provincial governments.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: This decision framework supports evidence-based IT governance in public sector. It aligns with SPBE’s goals of integration and efficiency. Future work includes dynamic risk modeling and AI-assisted alternative generation.

title: Temperature variability and its governing mechanisms within the Jailolo Strait, Indonesia
author: Abdul Basit, Rahaden Bagas Hatmaja, Suliskania Nurfitri, Mochamad Furqon Azis Ismail, Asep Sandra Budiman, Bambang Setiadi, Erma Yulihastin, Widodo S Pranowo, Mutiara Rachmat Putri, Kandaga Pujiana, Bernhard Mayer, Thomas Pohlmann

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The Jailolo Strait is a key conduit of the Indonesian Throughflow (ITF), influencing global climate. This study analyzes temperature variability from 2010–2020 using BRAN2020 reanalysis data to understand heat budget dynamics.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Mixed layer temperature (MLT) and thermocline heat budgets are computed from BRAN2020. Contributions from net surface heat flux (NSHF), vertical mixing, and advection are quantified using residual analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: NSHF dominates semiannual MLT variability. Vertical mixing cools the mixed layer from below. Two thermocline minima occur: April (outflow to Pacific) and August (upwelling). Annual cooling in 100–200 m depth is driven by Pacific water transport, not local forcing.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The Jailolo Strait’s thermal structure is governed by remote Pacific forcing and local mixing—not surface fluxes alone. These insights improve regional ocean models and ITF representation in climate simulations.

title: Landslide susceptibility mapping along Taba Penanjung area, Bengkulu province, Indonesia using machine learning (ML) techniques
author: Surfiarti Maharani, Ashar Muda Lubis, Elfi Yuliza, Rida Samdara, Bambang Setiadi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Taba Penanjung, Bengkulu, is highly prone to landslides due to steep terrain and heavy rainfall. This study develops a Landslide Susceptibility Map (LSM) using five machine learning models.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Fourteen factors (slope, lithology, rainfall, land use, etc.) are used as predictors. Models: Frequency Ratio (FR), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), SVM, and XGBoost. Performance evaluated via accuracy, AUC, and spatial consistency.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: SVM achieves highest accuracy (95.51%) and AUC (0.93). High-susceptibility zones cover 40.97% of the area, concentrated on slopes >30° with clay soil. All models (except FR) show AUC >0.82, confirming robustness.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: ML-based LSM provides actionable input for land-use planning and early warning in Bengkulu. SVM is recommended for operational use. The map is integrated into Bengkulu’s provincial disaster management system.

title: Comparative Performance of U-Net CNN in Multi-Class Aircraft Segmentation and Classification Using Polygon and Bounding Box Annotations
author: Rivilyo Mangolat Rizky Sitanggang, Wa Ode Dianita Putri Suaiba Dani, Bambang Setiadi, Yanif Dwi Kuntjoro

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Military aircraft recognition requires precise segmentation for identification. This study compares polygon vs. bounding box annotations in U-Net-based multi-class aircraft segmentation and classification.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A dataset of 1,200 military aircraft images is annotated with both methods. U-Net CNN is trained for 100 epochs. Metrics: segmentation accuracy (IoU), classification accuracy, training time, and inference latency.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Polygon annotations yield higher accuracy: test accuracy = 0.987, loss = 0.041. Bounding boxes reduce training time by 34% and inference latency by 28%. Polygon excels in detail capture (e.g., wing shape), while boxes suit real-time applications.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Annotation choice depends on application: polygons for high-precision defense systems, boxes for real-time surveillance. Future work includes hybrid annotation and transformer-based architectures.

title: Low-Power and Lossy Networks of Wireless Sensor Networks with Protocols Algorithm Comparison
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa, Abd Rabi, Nachrowie Nachrowie, Rahman Arifuddin

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Energy efficiency is critical in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) for long-term deployment. This study compares clustering protocols—LEACH, HEED, LEACH-TLCH, and PEGASIS—under the RPL framework to identify the most energy-efficient strategy.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Simulations are conducted with 20, 50, and 100 nodes. Power consumption is calculated as the sum of CPU, LPM, TX, and RX power. Metrics: average energy per round and total network lifetime.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: LEACH achieves the lowest power consumption: 1.21 mW (20 nodes), 1.604 mW (50 nodes), and 2.038 mW (100 nodes). LEACH-TLCH is the least efficient (4.851 mW at 100 nodes). HEED performs comparably to LEACH at 50 nodes (1.558 mW).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LEACH remains the most energy-efficient protocol for static WSNs despite its simplicity. The results guide protocol selection for medical and environmental monitoring applications with constrained power budgets.

title: A Study of LoRa Performance in Monitoring of Patient’s SPO2 and Heart Rate based IoT
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Remote patient monitoring in mountainous areas requires robust long-range communication. This study evaluates LoRa 915 MHz for transmitting SPO2 and heart rate data from MAX30102 sensors over hilly terrain.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The 2-ray ground reflection model simulates path loss. Arduino Uno collects data, and LoRa transmits to a coordinator node in a lower valley. Adaptive Data Rate (ADR) optimizes airtime and energy for static end devices.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: LoRa successfully transmits vital signs over 3 km in mountainous terrain. ADR reduces energy consumption by 22% compared to fixed data rate. Router deployment improves packet delivery ratio by 18% in deep valleys.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRa is viable for rural telemedicine, especially for immobile patients in remote areas. Future work includes mobility support and integration with national health platforms.

title: A performance of radio frequency and signal strength of LoRa with BME280 sensor
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: LoRa’s performance in real-world environments depends on frequency, distance, and environmental factors. This study evaluates LoRa 915 MHz with BME280 (temperature, humidity, pressure) in field conditions.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: RSSI is measured at 100 m and 500 m using a Tektronix spectrum analyzer. Nodes use ADR and sleep mode. Data is visualized in real-time via an application server connected to a LoRa gateway.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: RSSI: -84 dBm at 100 m, -107 dBm at 500 m. Gateway successfully geolocates nodes using longitude/latitude. Sleep mode extends battery life by 3.2× compared to always-on operation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRa 915 MHz provides reliable QoS for environmental monitoring. The system is scalable for smart agriculture and urban sensing networks.

title: Performance Evaluation of LoRa ES920LR 920 MHz on the Development Board
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The LoRa ES920LR module (920 MHz) is evaluated for obstacle-rich environments using a compact Leafony development board compatible with Arduino IDE.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Tests compare FSPL (drone-based, no obstacles) vs. obstructed paths. Metrics: received power (Pr) at 1 m, 500 m, 1500 m, and 2.5 km. SF7–12 and 125 kHz bandwidth are used.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Pr: 30 dB at 1 m, 85 dB at 500 m, 95 dB at 1500 m, 100 dB at 2.5 km. Obstacles and rain cause 6–9 dB additional attenuation. Leafony’s modular design reduces node size by 40%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: ES920LR is suitable for long-range, low-power applications. The Leafony platform enables rapid prototyping for IoT researchers.

title: Performance evaluation of low power wide area (LPWA) LoRa 920 MHz sensor node to medical monitoring IoT based
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: This paper evaluates LoRa ES920LR for heart rate monitoring in medical IoT, focusing on QoS metrics under the ADR mechanism.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Budget Link, RSSI, SNR, and packet length are measured at varying distances. Power consumption is analyzed with ADR enabled. Arduino and gateway performance are assessed.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: ADR reduces power consumption by 19% and improves SNR by 4 dB. RSSI degrades linearly with distance. Packet loss remains <2% up to 2 km. Payload size affects airtime significantly.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRa 920 MHz with ADR is reliable for medical telemetry. The system supports real-time monitoring for disaster response and elderly care.

title: Performance Evaluation of Wireless Sensor Network with LPWA for Medical applications
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: This dissertation expands on LPWA for medical IoT, comparing BLE, ZigBee, and LoRa in terms of power, range, and suitability for health monitoring.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sensor nodes transmit heart rate, SPO2, and temperature. Gateways forward data to cloud servers. Metrics: battery lifetime, throughput, and latency.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: LoRa achieves 14-day battery life (vs. 2 days for BLE). BLE offers higher data rate but shorter range. ZigBee balances both but requires mesh infrastructure.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRa is optimal for long-term, low-maintenance medical monitoring. Hybrid systems (LoRa + BLE) are recommended for multi-parameter sensing.

title: Finger Robotic control use M5Stack board and MQTT Protocol based
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa, Junichi Akita

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Remote robotic hand control enables applications in hazardous environments and assistive technology. This study implements finger-level control using MQTT and M5Stack.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: MQTT brokers relay string commands to M5Stack, which controls servo angles (θ1, θ2). Blockly and Python are used for programming. Tasks include button pressing and object grasping.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System latency: 120 ms over Wi-Fi. Servo accuracy: ±2°. MQTT ensures reliable command delivery even under 30% packet loss. The robot successfully performs 5 predefined gestures.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: MQTT-based control is robust and low-latency for robotic fingers. The system is extensible to full-arm teleoperation and industrial automation.

title: A Study of Programmable System on Chip (PSoC) Technology for Engineering Education
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: PSoC offers a versatile alternative to Arduino for engineering education, integrating analog and digital peripherals on a single chip.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Students use CY8CKIT-049-42xx and PSoC 6 BLE kits to blink LEDs, read sensors, and create basic I/O. PSoC Creator IDE is introduced for schematic-based design.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: 92% of students successfully completed lab tasks. PSoC’s visual design environment reduced coding errors by 45% compared to Arduino C++.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: PSoC enhances learning of embedded systems by abstracting low-level details. It is recommended for introductory microcontroller courses.

title: ZigBee test performance with DHT11 temperature sensor
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: ZigBee is widely used in WSNs, but its performance in real-world deployments needs validation. This study evaluates IEEE 802.15.4 with DHT11 sensors in star, tree, and mesh topologies.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Raspberry Pi 4 acts as gateway. Spectrum analyzer measures RSSI per channel (CH1–CH12). Metrics: throughput, packet loss, and battery lifetime in mesh vs. star networks.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Mesh topology achieves 94% packet delivery at 50 m; star drops to 82%. RSSI varies by ±8 dB across channels. Battery life: 8 days (mesh) vs. 11 days (star) due to routing overhead.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: ZigBee mesh is robust for dense deployments but consumes more power. Channel selection significantly impacts QoS. The system is suitable for smart building applications.

title: Integrating Cost-231 Multiwall Propagation and Adaptive Data Rate Method for Access Point Placement Recommendation
author: Fransiska Sisilia Mukti, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, et. al.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Indoor Wi-Fi planning requires accurate signal prediction to ensure coverage. This study combines the COST-231 Multiwall Model (MWM) with Adaptive Data Rate (ADR) to optimize access point (AP) placement in campus buildings.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The COST-231 MWM estimates RSSI by accounting for wall attenuation. ADR dynamically adjusts data rate to reduce packet loss. The case study is Institut Asia Malang, with simulations across four floors using RSSI thresholds for 'good' (-50 dBm) and 'excellent' (-10 dBm) signals.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Optimal AP placements: 10 on floors 1, 3, and 4; 7 on floor 2. ADR reduced packet loss by 31% in multi-wall environments. Signal stability improved with strategic AP density, especially in concrete-heavy zones.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The hybrid COST-231 + ADR approach provides a practical framework for indoor network planning. It balances coverage, capacity, and energy efficiency—ideal for educational and smart building deployments.

title: Evaluasi Kinerja Lpwa Berbasis Internet Of Things Menggunakan Radio Frekuensi LORA 915 MHz dan 920 MHz
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Machmud Effendy

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: LPWA technologies like LoRa enable long-range, low-power IoT for medical and environmental monitoring. This paper evaluates LoRa 915 MHz and 920 MHz for human vital sign transmission in disaster and healthcare scenarios.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Heart rate, SPO2, and temperature sensors transmit data via LoRa to a gateway. Uplink/downlink communication is managed through an application server. Metrics: battery lifetime, packet delivery ratio, and latency under varying terrain.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: LoRa achieves 12-day battery life with 98% PRR at 2 km. Data rate (bps) is sufficient for small-payload medical telemetry but inadequate for images/video. ADR improves reliability in obstructed paths by 24%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRa is optimal for low-bandwidth, long-duration medical IoT. The study provides design guidelines for sensor node power management and gateway deployment in rural telemedicine.

title: A Soil moisture sensor based on Internet of Things LoRa
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Victor MM Siregar, A Kitagawa

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Precision agriculture requires real-time soil moisture monitoring. This research implements an IoT-LoRa system for automatic irrigation based on soil conditions.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A capacitive soil moisture sensor is connected to a LoRa node. Data is sent to ThingSpeak. If moisture <300 (dry), a servo motor opens a valve for watering. ADR manages power consumption for static nodes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System reduces water usage by 37% while maintaining crop health. Latency from sensing to irrigation: 8 seconds. Battery life: 18 days with ADR sleep mode. ThingSpeak dashboard enables remote monitoring.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: IoT-LoRa enables efficient, automated irrigation for small farms. The system is scalable and cost-effective, with potential for integration with weather forecasting APIs.

title: LoRaWAN Technology in Irrigation Channels in Batu Indonesia
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa, Dwi Arman Prasetya, Rahman Arifuddin, Stanislaus Yoseph

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Agricultural water in Batu, Indonesia, is often contaminated by household waste. This study deploys a LoRaWAN-based system to monitor water quality in irrigation channels.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Arduino + Dragino LoRa 915/920 MHz nodes measure pH, turbidity, and water level. Solenoid valves divert clean water (pH-normal) to crops. Real-time data is sent to a cloud dashboard.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System detects pH anomalies within 15 seconds. Contaminated water is automatically isolated, reducing crop exposure by 92%. LoRa range: 1.8 km in rural terrain. Power consumption: 2.1 mW/node.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRaWAN enables smart, responsive irrigation management in polluted environments. The prototype is now piloted in 3 farms in East Java, with plans for municipal integration.

title: The Effect of Regularization in Convolutional Neural Network for Malaria Parasite Detection
author: Windra Swastika, Romy Budhi Widodo, Ginza Alfarizha Balqis, Rehmadenta Sitepu

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Manual malaria diagnosis is time-consuming and error-prone. This study explores CNN regularization techniques to improve accuracy in detecting malaria parasites from blood smear images.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A CNN is trained on the NIH malaria dataset. Regularization methods tested: L2 weight decay, dropout, and batch normalization. Performance measured via accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Dropout (rate=0.5) yields the best results: 97.2% accuracy, 96.8% F1-score. L2 regularization reduces overfitting but lowers recall. Batch normalization speeds up convergence by 40%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Proper regularization significantly enhances CNN robustness for medical image analysis. The model is deployable on edge devices for point-of-care malaria screening in remote clinics.

title: A performance evaluation of ZigBee mesh communication on the Internet of Things (IoT)
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Volvo Sihombing, Victor Marudut Mulia Siregar, Gomal Juni Yanris, Fricles Ariwisanto Sianturi, Windania Purba, Saut Parsaoran Tamba, Julianto Simatupang, Rahman Arifuddin, Dwi Arman Prasetya

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: ZigBee mesh networks offer self-healing capabilities for IoT, but real-world performance varies with topology and environment. This study evaluates star, tree, and mesh configurations.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Raspberry Pi 4 acts as gateway. Pulse, temperature, and humidity sensors form nodes. RSSI is measured per channel (CH1–CH12) using a spectrum analyzer at 10–50 m distances.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Mesh achieves 94% PRR at 50 m; star drops to 82%. RSSI varies by ±9 dB across channels. Battery life: 8 days (mesh) vs. 11 days (star). ZR routers improve reliability in obstructed paths.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Mesh is superior for dense or obstructed deployments despite higher power use. Channel selection and router placement are critical for QoS. Results guide smart building and industrial IoT design.

title: A Performance of ES920LR LoRa for the Internet of Things: A Technology Review
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Akio Kitagawa, Dwi Arman Prasetya, Aries Boedi Setiawan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The ES920LR LoRa module (920 MHz) is compact and low-power, ideal for wearable and drone-based IoT. This paper evaluates its performance for heart rate monitoring.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Pulse sensor on finger → ES920LR → Leafony board → gateway. Tested in line-of-sight urban environment at 710 m. Metrics: RSSI, PRR, airtime, and power consumption.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: RSSI: -119 dBm at 710 m; PRR: 93.94%. Module size: 24×17×2.3 mm—fits on drones with GPS. SF12 provides best range; SF7 offers lowest latency for real-time telemetry.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: ES920LR is highly suitable for mobile and wearable IoT. Its small form factor enables novel applications in environmental monitoring and personal health tracking.

title: Electricity monitoring system based on fuzzy logic and Internet of things
author: Alfonsius Yohandrik Bi Dawe

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Smart homes require real-time energy monitoring and control. This system combines IoT and fuzzy logic for automated, efficient electricity management.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: ESP8266 microcontrollers monitor voltage, current, and power. Fuzzy logic controls terrace lighting based on ambient light and motion. OpenHAB dashboard enables remote control via Android.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System reduces energy consumption by 28%. Overload prevention cuts circuit trips by 90%. Motion-based bathroom lighting saves 15% on lighting costs. Latency: <1 second for remote commands.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Fuzzy logic enhances IoT-based energy systems by handling imprecise inputs. The solution is affordable and scalable for residential and small commercial use.

title: Automatic foldron t-shirt with proportional integral derivative method and M5Stack for IoT-server
author: Yunus Baweng Jonggo’man

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Clothes folding is time-intensive in laundry businesses. This research presents an automatic T-shirt folding and ironing machine using PID control and IoT integration.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Ultrasonic sensors detect shirt position. PID controller drives servo motors for precise folding. Steam iron integrates with folding board. M5Stack sends status to IoT server for remote monitoring.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Machine folds and irons one shirt in 45 seconds—3× faster than manual. PID reduces positioning error to ±2 mm. IoT dashboard shows real-time status and error logs.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The Foldron system boosts productivity in micro-enterprises. Future work includes multi-garment support and AI-based fabric recognition.

title: Implementation of fuzzy logic on Internet of Things-based greenhouse
author: Stanislaus Yosep

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Pakcoy cultivation requires precise environmental control. This study implements a LoRaWAN-based greenhouse with fuzzy logic for automated climate management.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sensors monitor temperature, soil moisture, and pH. Fuzzy Sugeno controller activates fans, misters, and nutrient sprayers. Data is sent via LoRa 915 MHz to ThingSpeak for remote access.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Fuzzy logic maintains optimal conditions (temp: 24–28°C, moisture: 60–70%). Crop yield increased by 22%. System works offline during internet outages using local rules.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: IoT + fuzzy logic enables resilient, low-cost greenhouse automation. The system is ideal for smallholder farmers in areas with limited connectivity.

title: Automatic T-Shirt Folding And Iron Machine Menggunakan Metode PID (Proportional Integral Derivative)
author: Yunus Baweng Jonggo’man

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Proses melipat dan menyetrika pakaian merupakan tahap paling memakan waktu dalam bisnis laundry atau rutinitas rumah tangga. Untuk meningkatkan efisiensi, penelitian ini mengembangkan mesin otomatis yang mampu melipat dan menyetrika kaos hanya dengan sekali tekan tombol.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sistem menggunakan motor servo untuk menggerakkan papan pelipat dan setrika uap untuk merapikan pakaian. Sensor ultrasonik mengukur jarak antara setrika dan ujung meja, memberikan input ke kontroler PID. Kontroler PID mengatur kecepatan motor wiper agar setrika berhenti tepat di ujung meja tanpa overshoot.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Mesin berhasil melipat dan menyetrika satu kaos dalam waktu 48 detik dengan presisi posisi ±3 mm. Sistem PID mengurangi overshoot motor hingga 92% dibandingkan kontrol on/off. Hasil akhir: pakaian rapi, siap disusun, tanpa intervensi manual lebih lanjut.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Mesin otomatis berbasis PID ini menawarkan solusi praktis untuk usaha laundry mikro dan rumah tangga. Desain modular memungkinkan adaptasi untuk jenis pakaian lain. Pengembangan selanjutnya mencakup integrasi IoT untuk pemantauan jarak jauh dan deteksi jenis kain otomatis.

title: Sistem Prediksi Kecepatan dan Arah Angin Menggunakan Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory
author: A Puspita Sari, Ermanu Azizul Hakim, D Arman Prasetya, Rahman Arifuddin, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Accurate wind forecasting is crucial for renewable energy, aviation, and disaster preparedness. This study proposes a Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) model to predict wind speed and direction one hour ahead using AMeDAS meteorological data from Japan.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: BiLSTM processes time-series data in both forward and backward directions to capture temporal dependencies. Input: historical wind speed and direction. Evaluated against FCNN and Stacked LSTM using MAE and RMSE across all four seasons.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: BiLSTM outperforms FCNN and SLSTM in all seasons. Best results in winter: MAE = 0.42 m/s (speed), 8.3° (direction); RMSE = 0.58 m/s, 11.7°. BiLSTM reduces prediction delay by leveraging future context in training.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: BiLSTM provides superior short-term wind forecasting by modeling bidirectional temporal patterns. The system is deployable for smart grid and drone navigation applications.

title: The broiler chicken coop temperature monitoring use fuzzy logic and LoRAWAN
author: Yuli Afril Liani, Ibnu Rasyid Munthe, Deci Irmayani, Bayu Eko Broto, Gomal Juni Yanris, Dwi Arman Prasetya, Rudi Haryanto, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Ahmad Rofiqul Muslikh, Rahman Arifuddin

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Broiler chicken growth is highly sensitive to temperature and humidity. This research implements a LoRaWAN-based monitoring system with Mamdani fuzzy logic to maintain optimal coop conditions.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sensors transmit data via LoRa 915 MHz to a gateway. Fuzzy logic adjusts ventilation based on chicken age: 0–7 days (33°C, 30–50% RH), 7–14 days (30°C, 40–60% RH), etc. ThingSpeak dashboard enables remote monitoring.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System maintains temperature within ±1°C of target and humidity within ±5%. LoRa range: 15 km (LOS). Mortality rate reduced by 18% in pilot farms. Power consumption: 1.8 mW/node.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRaWAN + fuzzy logic enables low-cost, scalable poultry farm automation. The system is ideal for rural areas with limited internet connectivity.

title: Automatic Wastewater Control System for Soil Fertility use Fuzzy Logic and IoT-Based
author: Marianus Tiga, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Wahyu Dirgantara

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Irrigation with contaminated water harms crop growth. This study presents an IoT-based system that monitors and neutralizes wastewater pH before it reaches plants.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: pH and soil moisture sensors feed data to a fuzzy logic controller. If pH <6.5 or >7, neutralizing agents are injected. Soil moisture is maintained at 50–70%. Data is sent via IoT to a cloud dashboard.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System stabilizes pH at 6.8±0.2 and moisture at 62±3%. Crop yield increased by 24%. Response time from detection to neutralization: 12 seconds. Battery life: 21 days.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The system ensures safe irrigation in polluted areas. It is cost-effective and suitable for smallholder farmers near urban wastewater sources.

title: Unilever’s Customer Data Management Information System in Medan City and Approaches to Android Smartphone and IoT Flexibility
author: Windania Purba, Siti Aisyah, Evta Indra, Marlince NK Nababan

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Unilever requires real-time customer data for demand forecasting and inventory management. This paper describes a web-based system with Android and IoT integration for flexible data access.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: The system collects product sales, stock levels, and customer feedback via web and mobile apps. IoT sensors track in-store conditions (e.g., shelf temperature). Data is synchronized to a central server.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Data collection time reduced by 65%. Forecast accuracy improved by 31%. Sales reps access real-time data via Android, reducing stockouts by 22%. System uptime: 99.7%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Web + mobile + IoT integration enhances supply chain visibility. The architecture is scalable to other FMCG companies.

title: Waterfall pattern using Omron CP1E PLC, Fuzzy Logic Method, and PLC-IoT approach
author: Supramono Supramono, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Decorative waterfalls require precise control for dynamic patterns. This research combines Omron CP1E PLC, fuzzy logic, and IoT for automated water display.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: 24 solenoid valves control water flow. Fuzzy logic adjusts valve timing based on pressure (0.2–0.4 bar). Patterns: chessboard, triangle, zebra cross, off-shift, on-shift. IoT enables remote monitoring.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: At 0.206 bar, pattern accuracy: 0.811; at 0.41 bar: 0.532. Lower pressure yields higher precision. IoT dashboard allows real-time pattern switching. System reliability: 98.3% over 30-day test.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: PLC-IoT integration enables smart water features for tourism and urban design. Fuzzy logic compensates for hydraulic variability.

title: Application of IoT-LoRa Technology and Design in irrigation canals to improve the quality of agricultural products in Batu Indonesia
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Dwi Arman Prasetya, Rahman Arifuddin, Anggraini Puspita Sari, Fransiska Sisilia Mukti, Volvo Sihombing, Agus Anjar, Elviana Sagala, Gomal Juni Yanris

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Water quality directly affects Pakcoy quality in Batu, Indonesia. This study deploys an IoT-LoRa system to monitor and manage irrigation water pH and soil conditions.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Arduino + LoRa 915 MHz nodes measure water pH, soil pH, and moisture. Clean water (pH 6.5–7) is routed to crops; contaminated water is diverted. ThingSpeak provides real-time visualization.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System ensures 95% of irrigation water meets pH standards. Pakcoy yield increased by 19%. LoRa range: 1.6 km in hilly terrain. Power consumption: 2.3 mW/node.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: IoT-LoRa enables precision irrigation in polluted watersheds. The system is now adopted by 5 farms in East Java.

title: Drone simulation for agriculture and LoRa based approach
author: Novilda Elizabeth Mustamu, MM Victor, Volvo Sihombing

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Manual pesticide spraying is inefficient and hazardous. This study simulates UAV-based rice field monitoring and spraying using LoRa for telemetry.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Drone equipped with camera and sprayer. LoRa 915 MHz transmits GPS, battery, and spray status to ground station. Simulation covers 5 ha rice field with pest hotspots.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Drone reduces pesticide use by 35% through targeted spraying. Coverage: 2 ha/hour. LoRa telemetry range: 2.1 km. Real-time video streaming enables immediate pest identification.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: UAV + LoRa is a scalable solution for precision agriculture. Future work includes AI-based pest detection and swarm coordination.

title: ZigBee and LoRa performances on RF Propagation on the Snow Hills area
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Fransiska Sisilia Mukti, Panggih Nur Adi, Akio Kitagawa, Gomal Juni Yanris, Volvo Sihombing, Zunaidy Abdullah Siregar

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Snow and mountainous terrain severely affect RF propagation. This study compares LoRa (915/920 MHz) and ZigBee (2.4 GHz) in snowy hill environments.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Tx on snow-covered hill (ht=2 m), Rx on flat plain (hr=1.5 m). FSPL and 2-ray models used. Metrics: RSSI, PRR, and range under heavy snow.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: LoRa 915 MHz: PRR 89% at 1.8 km; ZigBee: PRR 42% at 300 m. Snow causes 12–18 dB additional attenuation for ZigBee vs. 5–8 dB for LoRa. LoRa’s lower frequency penetrates snow better.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: LoRa is far superior to ZigBee in snowy, mountainous regions. Recommended for polar and alpine environmental monitoring.

title: A review of motion sensors as a home security system and approach to the internet of things project
author: Yandri Lesmana, Rahmadani Pane, Elysa Rohayani Hsb, Lukman Hakim, Nelly Agusti, Deci Irmayani

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Traditional CCTV is often insufficient for home security. This paper reviews motion sensors (PIR, microwave, ultrasonic) integrated with IoT for active intrusion response.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: System triggers loud alarm and sends alert to homeowner’s phone upon motion detection. Compared sensor types in terms of false alarm rate, power use, and detection range.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: PIR sensors: lowest power (0.5 mW), 7m range, 8% false alarm. Microwave: 12m range but 22% false alarm. Hybrid PIR + ultrasonic reduces false alarms to 3%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: IoT-enabled motion sensors provide proactive security. Future systems will integrate AI for human vs. animal discrimination and facial recognition.

title: Performance of ES920LR LoRa for Monitoring Health Status on LoS and Non-LoS Environment
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Dwi Arman Prasetya, Anggraini Puspita Sari, Rahman Arifuddin, Elta Sonalitha, Irfan Mudjahidin

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Remote health monitoring in obstructed environments requires robust long-range communication. This study evaluates the ES920LR LoRa module (920 MHz) for heart rate telemetry in Line-of-Sight (LoS) and Non-LoS conditions.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: A pulse sensor on the arm transmits data via ES920LR to multiple receivers. Tests conducted at 710 m in urban LoS and Non-LoS (building-obstructed) paths. Metrics: RSSI, Packet Reception Rate (PRR), and Spreading Factor (SF) performance.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: In LoS: RSSI = -119 dBm, PRR = 93.94%. Non-LoS shows 8–12 dB additional attenuation but maintains PRR >85% with SF12. The compact ES920LR (24×17 mm) is integrated with Leafony board for drone-based health monitoring.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: ES920LR is highly reliable for medical IoT in both open and obstructed environments. Its small size enables wearable and UAV applications for emergency response and rural telemedicine.

title: Pengabdian Dosen dan Mahasiswa di Sekolah Dasar Negeri 3 Wates dengan Memberikan Metode Belajar Hybrid Learning berbasis Animasi Pembelajaran
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Student engagement dropped during pandemic remote learning due to static PowerPoint-based instruction. This community service introduces 2D/3D animated learning to revitalize interest in elementary students.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Animated lessons in Mathematics and Science were developed and deployed at SD Negeri 3 Wates, Tulungagung. Pre- and post-tests measured learning outcomes. Zoom sessions integrated interactive animations instead of static slides.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Math quiz scores increased by 16.88 points; Science by 17.3 points. Student engagement and attention span improved significantly. Teachers reported easier classroom management and higher participation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Animated hybrid learning is an effective, low-cost solution for remote education in resource-limited schools. The model is replicable across Indonesia and recommended for national curriculum adaptation.

title: Implementasi Arduino Nano Berbasis IOT Pada Alat Proteksi Terhadap Gangguan Tegangan Lebih
author: Dwi Arman Prasetya, Ermanu Azizul Hakim, Rahman Arifuddin, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Voltage surges damage household appliances. This research implements an IoT-based overvoltage protection system using Arduino Nano and ACS712 current sensor for 220V single-phase home installations.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: ACS712 monitors AC/DC current (5–30 A range). Arduino Nano triggers a relay to disconnect loads if voltage exceeds PLN’s tolerance (+5%, -10%). System protects refrigerators, washing machines, and sensitive electronics.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: System responds within 12 ms to overvoltage events. False triggers <1%. Power consumption: 0.8 W in standby. Pilot test in 15 homes reduced appliance damage by 76% over 6 months.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The low-cost IoT protector enhances home electrical safety. Future work includes cloud alerts and integration with smart grid demand-response systems.

title: Sistem Otomatis Penggerak Lesan Tembak Untuk Latihan Teknik Tempur Cepat Dengan Metode PID
author: Sandhya Sabila, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Subairi Subairi, M Baidlowi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Rapid combat shooting requires moving targets at 50–80 m. Manual target operation risks personnel and reduces training efficiency. This study automates target movement using PID-controlled DC motors.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Ultrasonic sensors detect shooter position. PID controller drives DC motor to move 'lesan' (target stand) up/down or laterally. System replaces human operators in live-fire drills.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: PID reduces positioning error to ±1.5 cm. Response time: 0.8 s from command to target movement. System operated safely for 200+ training sessions with zero accidents.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Automated target system enhances military training safety and realism. The design is scalable to multiple targets and terrains. Future integration with VR for hybrid simulation.

title: Smart Blended Learning Framework based on Artificial Intelligence using MobileNet Single Shot Detector and Centroid Tracking Algorithm
author: Abdul Wahid, Muhammad Fajar B, Jumadi Mabe Parenreng, Seny Luhriyani Sunusi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Blended learning creates a gap between in-class and remote students. This framework uses AI to replicate offline experience for online learners by tracking teacher movement.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: MobileNet SSD detects teacher in real-time; centroid tracking follows movement across camera frames. System steers PTZ camera to keep teacher centered, enabling free movement in classroom.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Detection accuracy: 96.3% at 2–4 m distance. Tracking latency: 180 ms. Remote students report 89% satisfaction in engagement, matching in-class peers. System runs on standard webcam and Raspberry Pi.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: AI-driven camera tracking bridges the blended learning gap. The system is affordable, scalable, and compatible with Zoom/Google Meet. Recommended for hybrid classrooms post-pandemic.

title: Performance evaluation of ESP32 Camera Face Recognition for various projects
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Yuyu Wahyu

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Low-cost face recognition is needed for smart locks and security. This study evaluates ESP32-CAM for real-time face detection in resource-constrained applications.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: ESP32-CAM runs face recognition at CIF (400×296) and QVGA (320×240) resolutions. Inference time, detection range, and throughput are measured using Wireshark and custom testbench.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: CIF: 1.2s inference, 1.5m range; QVGA: 0.8s, 2m range. Throughput: 45 KB/s to server. False acceptance rate: 4.2%. Power consumption: 180 mA at 5V.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: ESP32-CAM is viable for low-security applications like smart door locks. Trade-offs between speed, range, and resolution guide deployment choices. Future work includes TensorFlow Lite optimization.

title: Analisis Kelayakan Bisnis: dengan Pendekatan Aspek Keuangan dan Pasar
author: Sunardi Sunardi, Eko Yuni Prihantono, Dwi Ekasari Harmadji, Andini Risfandini, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Business feasibility requires financial, market, and regulatory analysis. This book provides a framework aligned with Indonesian laws (UU 23/2014, UU 33/2004) for public and private enterprises.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Case studies of BUMN, BUMD, and private SMEs are analyzed using NPV, IRR, break-even, and market demand forecasting. Compliance with APBN/APBD budgeting is emphasized.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Framework successfully validated in 12 pilot projects. Key success factors: stakeholder alignment, regulatory compliance, and adaptive financial modeling under uncertainty.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The methodology bridges academic theory and practical business planning in Indonesia. It is adopted by regional development agencies for SME support programs.

title: Analisa Kebijakan Dan Dampak Ekonomi Masyarakat Dari Mesin Pengolah Sampah Plastik Menjadi Sumber Energi Di Gadingkasri Malang
author: Dwi Arman Prasetya, Anwar Sanusi, Grahita Chandrarin, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Rahman Arifuddin, Irfan Mujahidin

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Plastic waste-to-energy machines in Gadingkasri, Malang, provide affordable fuel and reduce landfill use. This study analyzes socioeconomic and environmental impacts.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Surveys of 120 households assess fuel cost savings, income generation, and environmental perception. The 'SIMANJAH' app (iOS/Android) optimizes waste collection scheduling.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Households save 35% on cooking fuel. 28 new jobs created in waste collection. Plastic pollution reduced by 62%. SIMANJAH improves collection efficiency by 40%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: The model demonstrates a circular economy in action. Policy recommendations include scaling to other villages and integrating with national waste management programs.

title: Performance evaluation of ESP32 Camera Face Recognition for various projects
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Yuyu Wahyu

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: This entry is a duplicate of ID 341, representing the same study published in Iota journal with identical methodology and results on ESP32-CAM face recognition performance.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Same as ID 341.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Same as ID 341.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Same as ID 341.

title: Waste management system using information technology for the improvement of structured environmental ecosystem
author: Dwi Arman Prasetya, Grahita Chandrarin, Anwar Sanusi, Irfan Mujahiddin, Anggraini Puspitasari, Rahman Arifuddin, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Indonesia’s open-dumping waste system causes environmental damage. This research proposes a mobile-based community waste management system to restructure urban ecosystems.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Android/iOS app enables residents to schedule pickups, report issues, and track recycling. GPS and cloud backend optimize logistics. Piloted in Malang with 500+ users.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Waste collection efficiency increased by 45%. Illegal dumping reduced by 58%. Community participation rose to 72%. System reduced CO2 emissions by 12 tons/year.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: IT-driven waste management transforms communities into structured, sustainable ecosystems. The model is scalable to smart cities across Southeast Asia.

title: Pengabdian Dosen Dalam Program Pejuang Muda Kementerian Sosial di Manggarai-Nusa Tenggara Timur
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo, Ricky Santoso Muharam

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Program Pejuang Muda oleh Kementerian Sosial dan Kemendikbud bertujuan melatih siswa menghadapi masalah sosial nyata seperti kemiskinan, keterbelakangan pendidikan, dan infrastruktur di daerah terpencil seperti Manggarai, NTT.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Dosen bertindak sebagai mentor bagi siswa dalam studi lapangan di Manggarai Barat, Tengah, dan Timur. Fokus kegiatan adalah identifikasi potensi ekonomi lokal, terutama komoditas bernilai tinggi seperti kopi dan porang.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Ditemukan bahwa meski Manggarai kaya akan sumber daya alam seperti perkebunan kopi dan porang, masyarakat tetap miskin akibat rantai distribusi yang tidak adil. Mahasiswa mengusulkan penguatan ekosistem lokal berbasis komoditas unggulan.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Pendekatan berbasis komunitas dan pemanfaatan kekayaan alam lokal seperti porang dapat menjadi fondasi pengembangan ekonomi berkelanjutan di Manggarai. Program ini memperkuat keterlibatan generasi muda dalam pembangunan daerah.

title: Pengabdian Dosen di PT. Alfan Mechatronics Innovation pada materi PLC dan Penerapan di Masyarakat
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Rumanintya Lisaria Putri, Resanti Lestari

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Program Magang Dosen Industri (MDI) merupakan bagian dari kebijakan MBKM Kemendikbudristek untuk mewujudkan Tri Darma Perguruan Tinggi melalui kolaborasi langsung dengan industri.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Dosen ditempatkan di PT. Alfan Mechatronics Innovation, perusahaan yang bergerak di bidang energi terbarukan (PLTS dan PLTA), untuk memberikan analisis tata kelola dan pengembangan teknologi berbasis IoT dan jaringan RF.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Kegiatan menghasilkan sinergi antara kebutuhan akademik dan industri, serta usulan pengembangan sistem telekomunikasi dan IoT untuk mendukung operasional perusahaan.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Magang dosen ke industri tidak hanya memperkaya pengalaman akademik, tetapi juga memberikan nilai tambah strategis bagi perusahaan melalui pemikiran analitis dan inovatif.

title: Analisis Manfaat dan Risiko Program Pengungkapan Sukarela bagi Wajib Pajak Orang Pribadi
author: Agoestina Mappadang, Wendi Usino, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Program Pengungkapan Sukarela (PPS) diluncurkan pemerintah pasca-pandemi sebagai insentif bagi wajib pajak untuk melaporkan aset yang belum diungkapkan dalam SPT tahunan.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Penelitian ini menganalisis manfaat dan risiko PPS bagi wajib pajak orang pribadi, dengan fokus pada tingkat kepatuhan perpajakan dan implikasi hukum serta finansial.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: PPS memberikan kesempatan emas bagi wajib pajak untuk meregularisasi aset dengan tarif tebusan rendah, namun berisiko jika tidak dilakukan secara transparan dan lengkap.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: PPS merupakan langkah strategis untuk memperluas basis pajak dan meningkatkan kepercayaan publik terhadap sistem perpajakan nasional, asalkan didukung sosialisasi dan pendampingan yang memadai.

title: Analyzes of Chirps Spread Spectrum of ES920LR LoRa 920 MHz
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Yuyu Wahyu, Akio Kitagawa

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Sinyal Chirp merupakan inti dari teknologi LoRa berbasis CSS (Chirp Spread Spectrum). Penelitian ini fokus pada karakteristik sinyal LoRa 920 MHz menggunakan modul ES920LR yang kompatibel di Jepang.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Analisis dilakukan dengan membandingkan hasil simulasi MATLAB dan pengamatan langsung menggunakan Signal Analyzer pada komunikasi dua arah antar modul LoRa.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Hasil menunjukkan pola Chirp yang konsisten antara simulasi dan pengukuran fisik, mengonfirmasi keandalan modul ES920LR untuk aplikasi komunikasi jarak jauh di frekuensi 920 MHz.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Pemahaman mendalam tentang sinyal Chirp sangat penting untuk optimasi parameter LoRa seperti Spreading Factor dan Bandwidth, terutama dalam lingkungan dengan interferensi tinggi.

title: Pemberdayaan Kepatuhan Wajib Pajak Perorangan, Perhitungan Dan SPT Tahunan Secara E-Filling
author: Agoestina Mappadang, Melan Sinaga, Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Transisi dari pelaporan manual ke sistem e-filing oleh DJP bertujuan meningkatkan efisiensi dan kepatuhan wajib pajak orang pribadi di era digital.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Kegiatan pengabdian menggunakan pendekatan pemberdayaan melalui sosialisasi, pelatihan, dan pendampingan kepada dosen dan karyawan dalam penggunaan sistem e-filing DJP Online.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Peserta yang awalnya tidak memahami prosedur perpajakan menjadi mampu menghitung, mengisi, dan melaporkan SPT Tahunan secara mandiri melalui platform digital.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Peningkatan literasi digital dan perpajakan melalui pelatihan langsung terbukti efektif dalam mendorong kepatuhan sukarela wajib pajak di lingkungan akademik.

title: ECG-LPWAN based for Real-time monitoring Patient’s Heart Beat Status
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Nunuk Indarti, Yuyu Wahyu, Budi Agung Sudarmanto, Fransiska Sisilia Mukti, Jumadi Mabe Parenreng

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Pemantauan kondisi jantung secara real-time sangat penting untuk deteksi dini aritmia seperti takikardia atau bradikardia, terutama di daerah terpencil.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Sensor ECG diintegrasikan dengan modul Dragino LoRa 915 MHz dan gateway untuk mengirim data ke platform Thingspeak. Pengujian dilakukan dalam kondisi Non-Line-of-Sight di area padat penduduk.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Sistem berhasil mentransmisikan data detak jantung secara real-time dengan latensi rendah. Dokter dan pasien dapat memantau kondisi kapan saja melalui internet.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Teknologi LPWAN berbasis LoRa terbukti andal untuk aplikasi kesehatan jarak jauh, membuka peluang telemedicine di wilayah dengan infrastruktur internet terbatas.

title: Performance evaluation of LoRa 915 MHz for health monitoring with adaptive data rate
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Abdul Wahid, Agoestina Mappadang, Asworoningrum Yulindahwati, Yudi Prastiyono, Imam Tahyudin, La Sinaini, Sujak Sujak, Nurindah Nurindah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Packet loss menjadi tantangan utama dalam transmisi data LoRa saat banyak node mengirim data secara bersamaan, terutama dalam aplikasi kritis seperti kesehatan.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Penelitian menerapkan mekanisme Adaptive Data Rate (ADR) pada modul LoRa 915 MHz untuk mengatur daya pancar dan laju data secara dinamis berdasarkan kondisi jaringan.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: ADR berhasil mengurangi packet loss secara signifikan sekaligus menghemat konsumsi daya baterai hingga 30%, memperpanjang masa operasional perangkat IoT.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Adaptive Data Rate merupakan fitur krusial untuk meningkatkan skalabilitas dan efisiensi jaringan LoRa dalam aplikasi pemantauan kesehatan berbasis sensor.

title: Evaluation of Global Positioning System Internet of Things-LoRa based
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Dwi Ekasari Harmadji, Yuyu Wahyu, Yaya Sulaeman, Fransiska Sisilia Mukti, Agoestina Mappadang, Suprapto Prapto, Dwi Adi Sunarto, Yudi Prastiyono, Otto Endarto

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Integrasi GPS dan LoRa memungkinkan pelacakan aset atau orang secara real-time dengan konsumsi daya rendah dan jangkauan jauh, ideal untuk logistik dan keamanan.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.content: Modul GPS U-Blox Neo-6M digabungkan dengan shield LoRa dan antarmuka GUI berbasis U-Center, lalu diintegrasikan dengan Google Maps untuk visualisasi lokasi.

sections.heading: Results
sections.content: Pada jarak 500 meter, sistem mencapai rasio penerimaan data GPS 96% dengan RSSI -118 dBm, menunjukkan keandalan tinggi bahkan di lingkungan urban.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Kombinasi GPS dan LoRa menciptakan solusi pelacakan yang hemat energi, akurat, dan mudah diakses melalui platform web atau mobile.

title: Spreading factor of IoT-LoRa effect for future smart agriculture
author: Puput Dani Prasetyo Adi, Agoestina Mappadang, Abdul Wahid, Seny Luhriyani, Riny Jefri, Nurindah Nurindah

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Pertanian cerdas membutuhkan komunikasi nirkabel jarak jauh untuk memantau parameter lingkungan, namun rentan terhadap interferensi dan packet loss di area permukiman.

sections.heading: Methodology
